Specifically, SCProtoNet employs a dual-branch architecture to jointly process RGB and NIR images, effectively capturing phenotypic differences in soybean canopies caused by genotypes by optimizing prototype representations and contrastive learning instance discrimination based on few-shot scenarios. As a result, in the first year, SCProtoNet achieves an accuracy of 91.56% in a 1-shot training setting. In the second year, weights transferred from the first year are used to validate the generalization performance of the model across experimental years. Retraining the model in a 16-shot setting achieves experimental results of 87.65% and 100%. This few-shot learning model has been effectively tested on canopy images of 3232 different soybean genotypes. Experimental results demonstrate the robustness and generalization performance of the model across different experimental periods. SCProtoNet provides a valuable reference for implementing soybean genotype selection and lays the foundation for phenotypic analysis tasks in other crops under few-shot conditions. The source code and trained models are available at https://github.com/Lzylearn/SCProtoNet-Soybean.

title: Wintertime pollutant forecasting in northern sheep houses via a physics-constrained, multi-modal deep hybrid model
abstract: During winter in northern regions, the enclosed conditions of sheep houses result in poor ventilation, leading to the accumulation of pollutants, which severely impacts the health of mutton sheep. Realizing Precision Livestock Farming (PLF) necessitates high-precision forecasting models to transition management strategies from reactive responses to proactive, fine-grained interventions. To enable such proactive monitoring of the sheep house environment, this study proposes a deep hybrid model based on multi-modal fusion, FA-TMViT-XGB, for the prediction of indoor concentrations of NH3, CO2, PM2.5, and humidity specifically in enclosed sheep houses during winter. The study initially employs a sequential denoising strategy: Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) is utilized to adaptively separate high-frequency noise from valid signal modes, followed by Kalman filtering to robustly track the underlying trend state. Subsequently, in the temporal branch, a frequency attention module is introduced to focus on low-frequency periodic components, combined with trend decomposition, periodic modulation, and a TimeMixer network to extract multi-scale temporal features. Simultaneously, the time series are encoded into two-dimensional images via Gramian Angular Fields (GAF) and Markov Transition Fields (MTF), which are then input into a Vision Transformer (ViT) to extract spatial patterns. The extracted temporal and image features are fused through a gated mechanism, optimized with a physics-constrained heuristic regularization loss, and finally fed into an XGBoost regressor to generate the concentration prediction results.In the single-step prediction of NH3 concentration, the FA-TMVIT-XGB model demonstrated superior performance, achieving a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.0270, a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.0354, and an R2 of 0.9836 against the denoised reference trend. Crucially, robustness tests on raw sensor inputs confirmed the model’s resilience to high-frequency noise (R2>0.88). Compared to a pure Transformer model, the MAE and RMSE decreased by 73.6% and 70.8% respectively, and R2 increased by 21.8% Furthermore, multi-step forecasting experiments confirmed the model’s robustness (R2>0.9), serving as a supplementary safety buffer for risk warning. This complements the foundational single-step prediction, which satisfies the stringent precision requirements of PLF, enabling fine-grained ventilation adjustments to effectively prevent cold stress. By balancing immediate thermal stability with future air quality management, the model provides a comprehensive solution for improving flock health and production efficiency in wintertime enclosed sheep houses.

title: Detection of tea heat stress in UAV multi-spectral remote sensing images based on spatial-frequency two stream network
abstract: Accurate detection of tea heat stress (THS) using uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) multi-spectral remote sensing images combined with deep learning techniques is crucial for THS management. However, most existing multi-spectral image fusion detection networks lack robustness in complex scenes and perform poorly in small-target feature extraction, leading to low detection accuracy. To address these issues, a spatial-frequency two-stream network (SFTNet) is proposed. It employs spatial feature extraction (SFE) and frequency feature extraction (FFE) branches to extract high-resolution spatial details from RGB images and rich frequency-domain features from NIR images, respectively. A feature enhancement structure with multiple attention mechanisms and channel interaction was designed at the output end of the FFE branch to effectively aggregate shallow and deep semantic information from the hierarchically aggregated feature maps. For multi-scale feature fusion, a multi-spectral spatial-frequency feature fusion (MSFF) module is developed to achieve tight alignment and integration of RGB and NIR features. To improve small target detection, a multiscale cross-attention aggregation (MCA) module has been proposed. By extracting fine-grained horizontal and vertical features while incorporating a cross-fusion strategy, the MCA module enhances SFTNet’s learning of small target THS features, thereby improving detection accuracy for small target THS. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed SFTNet outperforms state-of-the-art networks across 4 m, 6 m, and 8 m datasets, achieving mAP@50 improvements of 5.9%, 7.7%, and 4.6% respectively. Furthermore, when evaluated on terminal devices in a non-deployment testing setup, SFTNet achieves an inference speed of 15.3 ms per RGB-NIR image pair, suggesting high computational efficiency under these specific conditions.

title: Research on an automated detection for sheep estrus based on multimodal fusion of thermal images and sensor data
abstract: Estrus monitoring is essential for improving reproductive efficiency and optimizing artificial insemination timing in ewes. However, existing studies mainly focus on binary estrus detection and often rely on wearable sensors, invasive physiological measurements, or vision-based behavioral analysis methods, which are insufficient for fine-grained estrus stage discrimination and are limited by animal stress, high deployment cost, and sensitivity to farm environmental disturbances. To address these limitations, this study proposes a non-contact multimodal framework for classifying ewe estrus stages into diestrus, estrus, and metestrus. Thermal infrared features were extracted using an improved ResNet18 incorporating initial convolution (INC), squeeze-and-excitation (SE), and multi-scale fusion (MSF) modules, denoted as INC-SE-MSF-ResNet18. In parallel, bilateral eye temperature features and environmental temperature and humidity features were extracted by multilayer perceptron (MLP)-based eye temperature feature extractor and MLP-based environmental variable feature extractor. These three types of features were then concatenated into a multimodal feature and classified using a Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM). Under the same LightGBM classifier, INC-SE-MSF-ResNet18 generated more discriminative thermal infrared features than ResNet18, MobileNetv3, EfficientNet, ShuffleNet, and DenseNet, yielding improvements of up to 15.10% in recall, 7.67% in F1-score, and 3.10% in accuracy. Under the same feature extraction and fusion strategy, LightGBM consistently outperformed support vector machine (SVM), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), gradient boosting decision tree (GBDT), random forest (RF), decision tree (DT), logistic regression (LR), and convolutional neural network (CNN) across all estrus stages, with precision improvements of up to 21.23% over CNN, 13.17% over DT, and 11.11% over RF. Temperature analysis further revealed clear stage-dependent divergence between bilateral eye temperatures and rectal temperature (RT). The bilateral eye temperatures peaked during estrus, whereas rectal temperature decreased during estrus and increased markedly during metestrus. These results indicate that surface and core temperatures reflect different physiological processes and exhibit unsynchronized temporal dynamics across the estrous cycle. Overall, this study extends infrared thermography-based ewe estrus monitoring from conventional binary detection to protocol-defined estrus stage classification, providing a feasible approach for ovulation timing inference and precision reproductive management in large-scale sheep farming systems.

title: Portable moisture-robust VNIR system integrating a PEPO algorithm for rapeseed chlorophyll quantification
abstract: Chlorophyll content is a critical determinant of rapeseed quality, significantly influencing the processing efficiency and oxidative stability of the resulting oil. However, moisture fluctuations during the harvest-to-processing cycle interfere with visible near-infrared spectroscopy, as moisture-induced spectral variance overlaps with chlorophyll spectral features. This study developed, a portable detection device for rapeseed analysis, and a partial external parameter orthogonalization (PEPO) method was implemented to reduce moisture interference. Compared to full-spectrum correction, PEPO uses a partial correlation analysis to calibrate moisture-sensitive wavelengths, aiming to retain target-specific spectral information. A comparison of machine learning architectures showed that an artificial neural network (ANN) combined with PEPO resulted in the highest predictive performance among the tested models. The model yielded a coefficient of determination in the prediction set of 0.891 and a root mean square error of prediction of 2.7 mg/kg. Relative to standard full-spectrum correction, the proposed approach reduced the performance gap between calibration and prediction sets, indicating improved model generalization. This study not only provides a technical basis for the rapid and non-destructive detection of rapeseed chlorophyll content but also offers an effective correction approach for the spectral analysis of complex agricultural materials susceptible to moisture interference.

title: Cypnet enabled spatiotemporal modeling of UAV hyperspectral imagery for wheat yield prediction and drought tolerant genotype identification
abstract: Accurate yield prediction and rapid identification of drought tolerant genotypes are critical for wheat breeding under increasing water scarcity. Despite recent advances in UAV based hyperspectral remote sensing and deep learning, a major unresolved challenge remains the robust modeling of high dimensional hyperspectral data across multiple phenological stages, particularly in large and genetically diverse breeding populations. Existing approaches often fail to simultaneously capture spatial spectral features, temporal dynamics of crop growth, and the unequal contributions of different growth stages to yield formation, limiting their applicability for breeding-oriented decision making. Here, we developed a hybrid deep learning framework, termed CYPNet, that integrates convolutional neural networks, bidirectional long, short term memory networks, and a multi head self-attention mechanism to enable end-to-end learning and adaptive temporal fusion of multi-temporal unmanned aerial vehicles(UAV)hyperspectral data. Field experiments were conducted using 535 wheat genotypes (262 recombinant inbred line families and 273 natural populations) grown under irrigation and water efficiency conditions in the Huang Huai Hai Plain. Canopy hyperspectral imagery was acquired at four key phenological stages (heading, flowering, early filling, and mid filling). Results showed that multi temporal spectral fusion substantially improved yield prediction accuracy, with CYPNet achieving the highest performance when all stages were integrated (R2 = 0.73, RMSE = 0.75 t/ha, MAE = 0.57 t/ha), outperforming traditional machine learning models, including optimized support vector regression (R2 = 0.62). Model performance exhibited environmental dependence, with slightly higher accuracy under irrigation than under water stress, reflecting increased spectral yield complexity under drought conditions. Importantly, yield predictions from CYPNet were further translated into a breeding-oriented decision framework by integrating drought resistance index, geometric mean productivity, and stress sensitivity index, enabling systematic ranking of drought tolerance across all genotypes. This framework identified 54 highly drought-tolerant wheat lines with stable performance and substantial yield potential, supported by high generalized heritability (H2 = 0.88). Collectively, this study addresses key methodological and application gaps in UAV based yield prediction by linking spatiotemporal hyperspectral modeling with quantitative drought resistance screening, providing a scalable and actionable phenotyping framework to accelerate genetic gain in wheat breeding under water limited environments.
keywords: Drought resistance screening of breeding varieties

title: Data fusion of Vis-NIR and pXRF with machine learning for predicting andic properties in volcanic soils
abstract: Volcanic soils exhibit distinctive andic properties, including organic carbon (OC), bulk density (Bd), phosphate retention (Pret), and the sum of ammonium oxalate-extractable aluminum and half iron (Alo + 0.5Feo), and play an important role in agricultural production and ecological functions. However, conventional determination of andic properties relies on destructive, labor-intensive, and time-consuming wet chemistry analyses. Soil spectroscopic techniques such as visible and near-infrared (Vis-NIR) spectroscopy and portable X-ray fluorescence (pXRF) provide rapid and non-destructive alternatives. This study aimed to elucidate the relationships between andic properties and signals from Vis-NIR and pXRF, and to evaluate the accuracy of sensor-based models for predicting andic properties and soil classification. A total of 93 soil samples were collected from 24 pedons of volcanic soils (0–60 cm depth) in northern Taiwan, including Andisols and Inceptisols. Predictive models were developed using individual sensors and a data fusion approach calibrated with partial least squares regression (PLSR) and the Cubist algorithm. Both Vis-NIR and pXRF signals demonstrated associations with andic properties, while data fusion of these two sensors markedly improved model performance. In particular, the Vis-NIR + pXRF-based model calibrated with Cubist yielded good predictive performance, achieving R2 and LCCC values exceeding 0.90 for OC, Pret, and Alo + 0.5Feo, and R2 = 0.83 and LCCC = 0.89 for Bd. Moreover, 23 out of the 24 studied pedons were correctly classified. Integrating Vis-NIR and pXRF provided an efficient approach for assessing andic properties, improving management and resource-use efficiency in volcanic soils, and supporting sustainable smart agriculture.

title: Transfer learning-based feature and token fusion for detecting grapevine yellows from multispectral images
abstract: Grapevine yellows diseases-most critically Flavescence Dorée, alongside Bois Nois-pose a significant threat to viticulture. Their symptoms are frequently confounded with those of Leafroll, Esca, and leaf discoloration, particularly in Chardonnay varieties, creating a complex multi-class classification challenge. To address this, we propose a transfer learning-based feature and token fusion method to detect grapevine yellows diseases from heterogeneous multispectral grapevine leaf images. The softmax-based fusion leverages probability distributions across multiple image features, tokens, and their merged combinations in a ’FUSION’ model. Feature and token extraction are performed using CNN and BEiT models, which are pre-trained on the ImageNet dataset and fine-tuned on our dataset. A lightweight ’HEAD’ classifier ensures efficient computation. Our approach can also be applied to classic RGB images. Evaluated on four datasets, including three public RGB benchmarks, the method achieved 100% accuracy on a 6-class subset and 99.954% on all 38 classes of PlantVillage, together with 100% on an open-source Grapevine Disease Dataset and 99.238% on another AI challenge dataset. On our challenging multispectral grapevine yellows dataset (5 classes: healthy, grapevine yellows, leafroll, discoloration, and Esca), it attained 82.87% accuracy on the same-year test data and a robust 79.99% on unseen-year data. These results outperform state-of-the-art approaches, highlighting the method’s potential for detecting diseases when symptoms are subtle, easily confused, or vary across acquisition years, including when using RGB images.

title: Interpretable ensemble learning facilitated digital mapping and driver assessment of soil available phosphorus
abstract: Soil available phosphorus is one of the key indicators of plant growth and soil fertility, and accurately and quantitatively mapping it is highly important. High-resolution soil mapping is necessary for soil management, but the applications of machine learning are still limited. The objective of the present study was to establish a stable and interpretable prediction model to map and explain the influence of environmental variables on the prediction of soil available phosphorus. Six machine learning models were tested at a spatial resolution of 30 m on the basis of data from 159 soil samples in North China, and ensemble models were established via the stacking method. Climate data, topography data, and remote sensing vegetation indices were used as inputs for the prediction of soil available phosphorus. The results showed that the ensemble models had higher accuracy than the machine learning models alone did, with a relative improvement of at least 33.3% in the coefficient of determination R2. The topographic variable dominated the prediction of soil available phosphorus, the climate variable affected the prediction in local areas, and the vegetation variable contributed to the prediction indirectly influenced by terrain and climate factors. Aspect, difference in vegetation indices and net primary productivity are the most important predictors. The variable selection based on multicollinearity analysis can improve the prediction accuracy and reduce the uncertainty of the ensemble model with an R2 increase of 4.51%, an RMSE decrease of 5.03% and an MAE decrease of 3.50%, but it may lead to a potential reduction in the extrapolation reliability, with the area of application decreasing by 4.84% and the potential loss of information for model interpretation. This study provides a data-driven approach for high-accuracy mapping and driver interpretation of soil properties.

title: LTF-YOLO: A lightweight framework for long-tailed agricultural pest detection in complex field environments
abstract: Early warning of agricultural pests is imperative for safeguarding crop yields, yet field-based pest detection remains challenging. Complex backgrounds, strict edge-computing constraints, and pronounced long-tailed class distributions impede reliable detection, especially for rare and visually similar pests. To address these challenges, this study proposes LTF-YOLO, a lightweight pest detection framework built on YOLO11n, designed to stabilize performance under long-tailed distributions in complex field environments. First, Pest Neighborhood Attention Transformer (PNAT) enhances feature robustness for tail-class and visually similar pests in cluttered scenes by strengthening local structural cues. Second, an efficient downsampling strategy (ADown) maintains a compact footprint suitable for edge deployment. Third, we propose Balanced-Proxy Loss (BP Loss) to mitigate long-tail-induced decision bias via class-frequency-aware logit reweighting and to improve boundary separation for underrepresented classes. Furthermore, we construct a multi-crop, cross-source pest detection benchmark, MultiCropPest-15 (MCP15), to support deployment-oriented evaluation under realistic long-tailed conditions. On IP102, LTF-YOLO achieves 57.4% mAP@0.5 and 36.0% mAP@0.5:0.95, improving by 4.4 and 2.2 points. On MCP15, it attains 77.7% mAP@0.5 and 47.0% mAP@0.5:0.95, improving by 7.2 and 5.2 points. An analysis across head, medium, and tail classes shows larger gains on tail classes, indicating effective mitigation of long-tail suppression. These findings highlight the significance of addressing long-tail-induced bias within a lightweight detection framework to ensure reliable and robust pest monitoring in agricultural environments.

title: IoT-enabled edge-based cattle behavior monitoring framework using TinyML and IMU sensor fusion
abstract: Continuous smart behavior monitoring is more essential to predicting early symptoms of cattle’s health issues in advance for modern livestock husbandry. Existing traditional and conventional approaches consume more time and labor and are often prone to errors. A cow’s health, feed factors, and environmental changes directly affect milk yield; farmers lose approximately ₹8,000–12,000 per cow annually due to nutritional imbalances and a lack of adequate early disease detection. This study proposes an integrated Internet of Things Machine Learning (IoT-ML)-based real-time precision cattle behavior recognition system. The wearable neckband device with an Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) sensor, micro SD card reader, and Quectel-GPS module that is interconnected with the ESP32 microcontroller, which is deployed on individual cattle, continuously acquires real-time sensor motions. To reduce unnecessary noise and placement disturbances while transitioning activities, the moving average filter (MAF) and extended Kalman filter (EKF) were applied to each IMU original sensor’s data. The integration of Hidden Markov Model (HMM) and Random Forest (RF) approaches delivered precise, robust motion prediction while transient activities occurred. The experimental findings showed a steady improvement in performance throughout the subsequent processing phases. The accuracy of the MAF pre-processing stage was 98.98%, whereas the EKF phase remained consistent at 98.65%. The final combined HMM-RF model achieved classification accuracy of 99.84% with an overall F1-score of 0.99 across the four behavioral classes. The proposed system employs a complete end-to-end pipeline (sensing → inference → IoT communication) on resource-constrained devices as ESP32 without cloud dependency, which is continuously, monitors the motion and behavioral patterns of cattle in real time so that farmers can easily identify early vital signs of diseases. Thereby, it prevents serious complications, reduces unexpected mortality rates, and provides a low-labor and low-cost solution to farmers, leading to increased overall farm productivity.

title: Robust covariance feature selection for unsupervised clustering of ultrasonic measurements on standing trees
abstract: Ultrasonic testing is a practical tool for health assessment of standing trees, but the resulting measurements are often affected by noise, heterogeneity, and outliers, complicating reliable interpretation. This study proposes Robust Covariance Feature Selection (RCFS), a label-free unsupervised feature selection framework that integrates Minimum Covariance Determinant-based Mahalanobis distances, sigmoid-based sample reweighting, and singular value decomposition-based cosine-squared feature scoring. A key contribution is a clustering-aware optimization framework in which mean cluster entropy is minimized via Bayesian optimization to jointly determine reweighting parameters, the number of selected features, and the number of clusters. The same entropy-based optimization strategy is also applied as a wrapper to Spectral Feature Selection (SPEC) and Unsupervised Discriminative Feature Selection (UDFS), representing spectral- and discriminative-based baselines. Validated on ultrasonic datasets from two Australian sites, RCFS achieved accuracy gains of 4%–8%, normalized mutual information gains of 30%–45%, Silhouette improvements of 20%–45%, and entropy reductions of 50%–70% relative to the baseline methods, while also producing stable feature subsets under resampling. Ablation studies on COIL20 and ORL, including comparison with Unsupervised Soft-Label Feature Selection (USFS), further show that the proposed reweighting improves performance when outlier influence is pronounced while remaining effectively neutral when such influence is limited, thereby preserving the underlying data structure for feature ranking.

title: Assimilation of LAI and FAPAR within DSSAT guided by leaf growth dynamics to enhance maize yield phenotyping
abstract: Maize (Zea mays L.) yield phenotyping is essential for breeding high-yielding cultivars and addressing global food security challenges. However, because yield accumulates throughout the growing season and is shaped by complex genetic, physiological, and environmental interactions, accurate yield phenotyping remains challenging. Traditional yield phenotyping is labor-intensive, limited to harvest-stage assessment, and unable to capture the dynamic processes underlying yield development. The emergence of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-based hyperspectral high-throughput (HTP) phenotyping provides a non-destructive, large-scale, and temporally continuous approach. These HTP data are commonly analyzed using machine learning (ML) models to extract yield-sensitive features and establish relationships with historical yield labels for prediction, whereas such models often remain limited in physiological consistency, interpretability, and performance stability. To address these limitations, a UAV-based data assimilation framework, HyperDA-Leaf, was developed to dynamically integrate weekly UAV-derived leaf area index (LAI) and fraction of absorbed photosynthetically active radiation (FAPAR) into the Decision Support System for Agrotechnology Transfer (DSSAT) for yield phenotyping. HyperDA-Leaf integrates a data exchange interface within DSSAT, enabling the coupling of leaf area dynamics with UAV-based data assimilation to generate physiologically realistic and observation-constrained growth trajectories for improved yield prediction. Results showed that HyperDA-Leaf produced daily LAI and FAPAR trajectories with fewer unrealistic fluctuations and exhibited stronger correlations with daily radiation and temperature. HyperDA-Leaf also achieved robust performance across three years in breeding-oriented experimental fields containing thousands of maize hybrids, achieving high yield prediction accuracy (R2 > 0.6) without using yield labels and outperforming comparative ML models. Furthermore, the optimized light stress factor (LSF) enhanced physiological interpretability by showing that high-yielding hybrids experienced lower light stress intensity and fewer stress days, owing to their greater photosynthetic efficiency, as reflected by higher LAI and FAPAR values. Overall, HyperDA-Leaf provides a physiologically grounded, interpretable, and robust solution for UAV-based maize yield phenotyping, supporting the understanding of maize yield formation and large-scale breeding applications.

title: Adaptive rotary tillage depth control with RBF-ADRC based on time-series prediction of tractor chassis pitch angle
abstract: To mitigate tillage-depth fluctuations induced by surface undulations and actuator nonlinearities in horticultural electric tractors, this study develops a predictive depth control method. A novel MSCNN–BiLSTM–Attention model is constructed to forecast pitch-angle variations. It utilizes multi-scale convolution to extract disturbance features across different temporal scales, while bidirectional temporal modeling combined with a multi-head attention mechanism enhances temporal representations. Model hyperparameters are optimized using an improved beluga whale optimization algorithm. The predicted pitch angle is integrated as feedforward compensation into the control loop. By fusing this prediction with a rotary-tillage kinematic model, future tillage depth is estimated, enabling the design of an RBF-based active disturbance rejection controller (RBF-ADRC) for adaptive compensation of system nonlinearities and time-varying disturbances. The proposed prediction model achieved MAE and RMSE of 0.0526° and 0.0686°, respectively, with a test-set R2 of 0.9931, and errors primarily within ± 0.03°. Simulations demonstrated that the proposed prediction-assisted control strategy outperforms RBFPID, optimal sliding mode, and model predictive controllers under step, sinusoidal, and slope disturbances, achieving zero overshoot, a steady-state error of 0.001 cm, and reduced dynamic errors. Greenhouse field experiments further validated the method, yielding average tillage depths of 4.03, 8.14, and 11.59 cm against targets of 4, 8, and 12 cm, with maximum fluctuations of approximately 0.6 cm. Overall, this deep learning-based predictive feedforward strategy significantly improves tillage-depth stability and control precision under complex surface conditions, providing a practical solution for intelligent electric tractors in protected horticulture.

title: Haar wavelet-guided dynamic Feature Pyramid Network for an efficient paddy leaf disease classification
abstract: Early and accurate identification of paddy leaf diseases is crucial for timely intervention and effective crop management. Although deep learning based approaches have demonstrated strong performance in paddy leaf disease classification, they often struggle to capture the diverse multiscale symptom patterns of diseases, resulting in the misclassification of challenging samples. Moreover, the high computational cost of deep learning based models remains a significant limitation. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel Haar wavelet-guided deep Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) model. In the proposed framework, deep features are extracted using a backbone network, and a FPN is employed to capture multiscale disease symptoms. In parallel, Haar wavelet features are extracted to provide complementary texture cues that are not explicitly modelled by deep features. Guided by these wavelet features, a gating-based dynamic feature selection module is then utilised to identify image-specific FPN features, which are subsequently used for classification. In the second phase of the study, a lightweight variant of the proposed model is developed using a knowledge distillation technique, achieving high classification accuracy while substantially reducing the number of parameters and FLOPs. In addition, a new benchmark dataset, named NP-LankaPaddy, is constructed to address the limited availability of datasets representing Sri Lankan paddy leaf disease conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that both the proposed approach and its lightweight variant outperform state-of-the-art methods across four benchmark datasets, achieving notably high accuracies of 98.04% and 97.84%, respectively, on the well known Paddy Doctor dataset. The source code and dataset supporting this study are openly available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18334503.

title: Addressing representation instability, strategy rigidity, and class imbalance in active learning for agricultural pest and disease recognition
abstract: Agricultural pests and diseases cause substantial crop losses worldwide, yet deploying deep learning in smart agriculture is hindered by the high cost of expert annotation. Generative AI (GAI) techniques such as GANs can augment training data, but generated samples still require expert verification and their quality depends on real labeled data, leaving the annotation bottleneck unresolved. Active learning offers a complementary solution by selecting the most informative samples for labeling, yet existing methods suffer from three limitations: representation instability due to static prototype computation on noisy field images, strategy rigidity from fixed selection ratios across training stages, and neglect of class imbalance during sample selection. We propose a three-level active learning framework that introduces targeted innovations at each level of the learning pipeline. Dynamic Prototype Memory maintains stable class representations through momentum-based exponential moving average updating, providing provably lower variance than static prototype recomputation. Context-Aware Sample Selection employs a neural contextual bandit to dynamically adjust the branch combination ratio at each round, learning how to combine complementary selection strategies rather than which individual samples to select. Class-Balanced Scoring incorporates inverse-frequency weighting to prioritize underrepresented classes directly at the selection stage, filling a gap left unaddressed by existing active learning methods. Experiments on IP06 (insect pest) and Natural CW-10 (weed) datasets demonstrate that the framework achieves 83.36% and 85.07% accuracy at 90% data availability, outperforming the strongest competitor by 4.12 percentage points on IP06 and 2.68 percentage points on Natural CW-10 at 20% data availability, with the largest gains concentrated in low-data regimes. Integration with GAN-augmented data yields further additive improvements, with combined accuracy reaching 84.91% on IP06 and 86.42% on Natural CW-10, confirming the complementary role of active learning within GAI-empowered smart agriculture pipelines. These results demonstrate that principled annotation selection can substantially reduce labeling costs while maintaining competitive recognition performance, offering a practical and scalable solution for real-world smart agriculture deployment where expert annotation resources are severely constrained. Ablation studies verify that the three innovations are mutually complementary, and sensitivity analysis shows robustness to hyperparameter variation.

title: Fusing hyperspectral, meteorological, and irrigation data for simultaneous estimation of soil and leaf water status via ensemble learning
abstract: Accurate and simultaneous estimation of leaf equivalent water thickness (EWT) and soil water content (SWC) remains challenging due to spectral interference between canopy and soil signals. This study aims to develop a regression framework for simultaneous estimation of SWC and EWT from a single hyperspectral observation by fusing disentangled spectral features with meteorological and irrigation data. We employed Recursive Feature Elimination method to select sensitive spectral matrices (SSMs) for EWT and SWC, respectively. Spectrum fusion and decomposition of the SSMs using the Non-negative Matrix Factorization and linear subtraction methods, which yields the moisture spectral feature matrix (MSFM). The MSFM combined with meteorological and irrigation indicators, were used as inputs for five base machine learning regressors. Their outputs were further optimized using ensemble algorithms, including Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) and Bagging. The effectiveness of the above method in estimation EWT and SWC were tested with field experiments on different irrigation levels, film mulching treatments, and maize varieties in the Shiyang River Basin of Northwest China during 2021 and 2022. The results show that MSFM combined with meteorological and irrigation indicators yield highest prediction accuracy for EWT/SWC compared with MSFM, SSM or full spectrum. Among the five base regression algorithms, Random Forest regression yielded the highest estimation accuracy for SWC, while Multi-Layer Perceptron regression showed superior performance in estimating EWT. Both ensemble algorithms enhanced the testing accuracy of SWC and EWT compared with the five base regression algorithms, improving the coefficient of determination (R2) by 10.84–46.89%, and reducing the root mean square error (RMSE) and normalized RMSE (NRMSE) of 6.87–33.27%. Additionally, under the tested conditions, EWT and SWC errors remained below 28% when leaf area estimation errors were under 25%. This study demonstrates the potential of a unified modeling framework using a single set of hyperspectral observations to accurately estimate crop and soil moisture status under mixed soil–canopy conditions.
keywords: Purification of soil and crop moisture spectrum

title: FishKeypoints: A comprehensive stereo vision framework for fish behaviour monitoring and size measurement in aquaculture
abstract: The shift towards Precision Fish Farming (PFF) requires reliable, automated tracking of individual fish in dense, dynamic underwater environments. Many approaches targeting this topic are based on using computer vision methods and AI to detect and track the fish automatically. Most conventional approaches rely on the use of Horizontal Bounding Boxes (HBBs), however this approach has proven inadequate for accurately localising slender fish with variable orientation, particularly in scenes where fish density and occlusion is high. This study presents a new computer stereo vision framework that leverages Oriented Bounding Boxes (OBBs) for fish detection followed by keypoint detection for the localisation of the anatomical features of the detected fish. The method was set up to directly estimate 3D positions of the detected fish and keypoints and track these over time without external calibration targets. When applied to stereo video data collected from two field trials at commercial fish farms, the method estimated fish-camera distances and fish lengths that corresponded with reference data obtained through other sensors and manual sampling. These results imply that this new approach represents a step forward in non-invasive, automated monitoring and analysis of fish behaviour and growth, giving more detailed insights into farmed fish dynamics and contributing to further progress in the realisation of PFF.

title: Light-TDNN: A lightweight acoustic model for panic stress recognition of caged laying hens in intensive farms
abstract: Panic stress is a prevalent environmental stressor in laying-hen production, leading to severe consequences such as weakened immunity and reduced egg production. Traditional monitoring methods, including manual inspection and physiological sampling, are labor-intensive and invasive; moreover, blood sampling itself may induce secondary stress. Video-based monitoring is also constrained in intensive battery-cage systems due to severe visual occlusion. In contrast, acoustic signals are well suited to complex cage environments because of strong penetration, flexible deployment, and high information density. Leveraging these advantages, a lightweight panic stress vocalization recognition model, the Lightweight Time Delay Neural Network (Light-TDNN), was constructed. To support model development and evaluation, an acoustic dataset collected under diverse typical stressor stimuli was established. Built upon the TDNN architecture, Light-TDNN integrates three key optimization strategies: (1) a Dilated-Shuffle module that substantially reduces model size while capturing long-range temporal dependencies via an expanded receptive field; (2) a Time-Frequency attention module that focuses on the most discriminative time–frequency features and enhances the recognition of easily confused sounds like panic-induced cage noise and feeding sounds; and (3) a relational knowledge distillation strategy that transfers teacher model knowledge and elevates the student model’s performance ceiling without increasing inference cost. Experiments in real farming scenarios show that Light-TDNN achieves a precision of 96.44% and a recall of 93.75%, with only 0.34 M parameters and 39.86 M FLOPs, delivering a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off compared with mainstream models. Additionally, a real-time monitoring system was developed by deploying Light-TDNN on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin edge architecture. The system achieves an average end-to-end latency of 23.89 ms per 4-s window, enabling low-latency real-time monitoring in large-scale farms. This work offers a robust on-device solution for non-invasive stress detection, providing a quantitative metric to assess the welfare compatibility of intelligent agricultural machinery and inform welfare-oriented equipment design.

title: Graphs that know who started it: Role recognition in Pigs’ interactions
abstract: Social interactions among group-housed farm animals are important welfare indicators in housing systems. Computer vision approaches are emerging as important tools to detect, classify, and quantify interactive farm animal behaviors. However, because of their focus on appearance features (e.g. background, motion blur, etc.) convolutional recurrent neural network approaches struggle to capture the complex, role-specific dynamics of one-to-one interactions such as fighting, feeder displacement, and tail biting, among others, often capturing only the distinction between fast-moving and slow-moving behaviors. In this study, we propose a graph-based neural network (HeteroGNN) to model and classify both spatial and temporal relationships among key body landmarks of interacting pig pairs. Our method encodes a carefully engineered set of kinematic features into a graph structure, effectively capturing behaviors expressed through various movements over different durations. The model simultaneously classifies the interaction category (e.g. tail biting) and predicts individual roles (aggressor vs. victim) through a hierarchical two-level classification allowing targeted intervention for aggressors or victims. Validation of the model demonstrated good performance in behavior recognition, achieving an average F1-score of 94%. It was also able to demonstrate strong capabilities in discerning the role of each individual in one-to-one interactions, with an average F1-score of 90%. Testing on unseen farm environment yielded better generalization performance than a convolutional recurrent neural network (CRNN) model. Specifically, the CRNN, which relied on appearance features, experienced a 50% performance drop from validation to test environments, whereas our approach showed only a 12% drop. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of graph-based representations in discerning asymmetric interactions in pigs. Our framework lays the groundwork for more nuanced, role-aware animal welfare monitoring systems. More information and data are available at: M3-BIORES/Public/M3PIG·GitLab.

title: Knowledge-informed Gaussian process regression with agronomic priors for variable-rate nitrogen management in cereal crops
abstract: Empirical response curves often oversimplify yield-nitrogen (N) dynamics, while purely data-driven models like extreme gradient boosting (XGB) can be physically implausible and provide limited uncertainty guidance. A more reliable approach is needed, one that is both accurate and consistent with agronomic laws. This study introduces a knowledge-informed Gaussian process regression (KI-GPR) model that embeds a quadratic yield-N relationship within a Bayesian Gaussian process, adapting the law of diminishing returns and acknowledging toxicity at excessive N rates while learning from soil covariates. The study uses on-farm precision experimentation (OFPE) datasets from four arable fields in Flanders with soil properties measured by an online visible and near-infrared (vis-NIR) spectra sensing platform and laboratory analyses. Three models are compared, namely, a clustered empirical quadratic, a purely data-driven XGB regressor, and the proposed KI-GPR that learns soil-dependent parameters while constraining the response with agronomic priors. All three models are evaluated and compared using both statistical (coeffecient of determination [R2] = 0.86; root mean square error [RMSE] = 0.024 kg kg−1; and ration of performance to interquartile distance [RPIQ] = 3.920) and agricultural metrics (N-response curves and marginal yield curves). KI-GPR is found to outperform both empirical polynomial model (EMP) and XGB models, producing smooth, agronomically credible response curves and continuous optimal-N distributions. It also provides uncertainty quantification, which enables risk-aware recommendations and highlights data gaps. The approach is well-suited for variable-rate N management, decision support, and targeted experimental design.

title: An innovative approach to SCC prediction in cow’s milk using a low-cost RF/MW dielectric probe combined with DWT-CNN model
abstract: The key to online detection of somatic cell count (SCC) in cow’s milk based on radio frequency/microwave technology lies in reducing the cost of dielectric probes and improving model accuracy. This study proposed a quantitative method for milk SCC using a low-cost helix-electrode dielectric probe (HEDP) combined with a deep learning model. However, the influence of SCC on the milk S-parameter spectrum measured by HEDP and the predictive accuracy of this method remain unclear. The S-parameter spectra (20-4500 MHz) of milk samples with different SCC were measured with HEDP. Subsequently, the influence of SCC on the S-parameter spectrum (S11, S21) and their correlation characteristics were analyzed. A novel convolutional neural network (CNN) model integrating the discrete wavelet transform (DWT) was developed to predict milk SCC. The results indicated that the electromagnetic coupling between the HEDP and milk exhibited multiple-resonance characteristics. At the resonance frequencies, SCC showed positive and negative correlations with S11 and S21 spectra, respectively. A strong nonlinear relationship was observed between SCC and the S-parameter spectra (APaRPs: |Z|=8.571). The DWT-CNN model outperformed both CNN and chemometric models. The HEDP combined with DWT-CNN for milk SCC detection achieved good performance (RMSE: 0.163 log SCC/mL, RPD: 2.51). This method was low-cost and high-precision, and the probe was easy to calibrate and clean, making it suitable for online SCC detection. This study provided a new insight into the low-cost online detection of milk SCC and monitoring of mastitis in dairy cows.

title: Soft semantic grouping and feature clustering for panoptic segmentation of tree crowns and trunks in LiDAR point clouds
abstract: High-throughput tree growth phenotyping depends on acquiring structural information. LiDAR-based point clouds enable 3D quantitative morphological analysis, but accurate crown–trunk segmentation is an essential prerequisite for extracting reliable phenotypic parameters and enabling subsequent high-precision phenotyping analysis. However, traditional 2D image analysis methods are limited by dimensional constraints, failing to quantify 3D structural features of crowns. The irregularity, sparsity, and noise of LiDAR point clouds cause traditional geometry-dependent algorithms to extract features with insufficient accuracy. Besides, difficulties in assigning instance labels in overlapping crown edges and semantic ambiguity in crown–trunk transition zones further exacerbate segmentation errors. Existing deep learning methods exhibit poor generalization and robustness, yielding inconsistent performance across multi-platform and heterogeneous forest point clouds. Currently, no unified panoptic segmentation framework exists that concurrently resolves crown–trunk semantic ambiguity, adapts to substantial LiDAR platform-specific point density variations, and accurately delineates instances in densely overlapping forest canopies. To address these, this work proposes the crown–trunk Segmentation (CTS) panoptic framework. A soft semantic grouping module resolves transition zone ambiguity by assigning points to multiple categories, and a feature clustering-deformable convolution module shifts canopy points to centroids, overcoming overlapping instance labeling issues. Validation on multi-platform point cloud datasets shows that the proposed CTS achieves a semantic segmentation overall accuracy of 88.15% and an instance segmentation F1 score of 99.31% in both mature and young forests. Ablation studies confirm significant synergistic gains from the soft semantic grouping and feature clustering modules. Comparisons on the public FOR-instance dataset show 8.7 average F1 score improvement over Point2tree and ForAINet, with 13.22 recall gain in complex overlaps. Extracted growth phenotyping parameters (trunk DBH RMSE 0.021, 3D crown area 6.354) demonstrate the potential of volume-area correlation analysis, and the improved segmentation accuracy could facilitate downstream 3D growth analysis as a potential application.

title: Variational autoencoder enables unsupervised leaf diagnosis via hyperspectral imaging
abstract: Hyperspectral imaging provides rich spectral information for plant phenotyping, yet analyzing these high-dimensional data remains challenging due to limited labeled datasets and the reliance on manually extracted features, such as vegetation indices. Here, we present LeafVAE, a variational autoencoder framework that learns spectral signatures directly from hyperspectral leaf images without manual annotation. Our model encodes leaf spectra into a compact, two-dimensional latent space where pixels cluster by spectral similarity, creating quantitative leaf descriptors from signature composition that facilitate downstream phenotyping tasks. We show that the learned representations generalize robustly across genotypes, years, and imaging equipment on four different corn leaf datasets. We further demonstrate that LeafVAE outperforms traditional vegetation indices across multiple applications, including detecting nitrogen deficiency in corn, classifying herbicide stress in soybean, and identifying beech leaf disease using an affordable six-band multispectral camera. Pixel-level explainability, achieved by combining spectral signature composition with interpretable machine learning methods, identifies regions with abnormal spectral characteristics and highlights areas of the leaf that contribute to model predictions. By learning spectral features in an unsupervised manner while still allowing labels for interpretable diagnosis, LeafVAE provides a scalable foundation for automated plant phenotyping across diverse applications.

title: A multisource weakly supervised high-resolution crop mapping framework based on low-resolution noise labels
abstract: High-resolution (HR) crop maps are the foundation data for conducting precise agricultural monitoring and land use change analysis. However, HR crop mapping remains hindered by costly manual annotations, label noise from low resolution (LR) products, convolutional neural network (CNN) architectural limitations, and spatial-spectral constraints of single source remote sensing imagery. LR crop classification products serve as cost-effective weak supervision but introduce geometric and semantic label noise. Conventional CNNs struggle with preserving fine spatial details and modeling long-range contexts, while data-level multi-source fusion blurs parcel boundaries. To address these issues, we propose a multisource weakly supervised crop classification framework (MSWCF) that utilizes LR products to guide HR mapping. The MSWCF features dual parallel branches: the HR branch extracts parcel boundaries, while the LR branch captures semantic information. Each branch integrates spatial resolution preserving and Vision Transformer modules to concurrently extract local details and global contexts. A cross-attention module (CAM) adaptively fuses these features, while a noise label removal module suppresses boundary and semantic errors in LR labels. Experiments were conducted in Heilongjiang Province, China. Results show that MSWCF achieves superior performance (Overall Accuracy = 93.8 %) surpassing state-of-the-art baselines. Cross-spatiotemporal application indicates that it has generalization capabilities. Ablation studies confirm that the dual-branch structure and CAM fusion effectively utilize spatial-spectral information, preventing boundary smoothing. Feature visualization verifies that SRP focuses on boundaries while ViT captures global objects. MSWCF enables accurate, fine-grained crop mapping without manual annotations, validating its practicality for largescale HR crop mapping.

title: Dead pine tree detection using an iterative semi-supervised framework integrating expert annotation and active learning
abstract: Pine wilt disease (PWD) poses a severe threat to forest ecosystems and resources, and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) remote sensing combined with deep learning (DL) has become a widely used approach for its detection. However, DL-based methods typically rely on large-scale labeled datasets, while semi-supervised learning (SSL) still faces a key limitation in practice: the lack of a principled strategy for determining optimal annotation ratios, often leading to either insufficient supervision or unnecessary labeling cost, and existing static training schemes fail to adapt to dynamically evolving data distributions. To address this gap, we propose a human–machine interactive framework that integrates active learning (AL) with SSL through interactive training and expert-driven annotation. An AL method, object uncertainty sampling (OUS) strategy was employed to enhance annotation efficiency. Our results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves detection accuracy comparable to fully supervised approaches while using only 30 % of the labeled data (mAP = 64.9 %, mAP50 = 94.1 %), and improves performance by 3.1 %–11.4 % in mAP compared with other SSL methods. Moreover, when applied to new datasets, this method supports transfer learning, allowing the model to retain prior knowledge while improving performance on new data, with mAP and mAP50 reaching 55.32 % and 93.3 %, respectively. By integrating automated learning with expert judgment, it reduces manual effort and achieves optimal detection with minimal annotation. Additionally, the proposed strategy exhibits cross-model generalization and can be combined with multiple object detection models, including SSD, YOLOv12, and DETR, enhancing the performance of baseline models while reducing annotation requirements. This approach offers a novel perspective on PWD detection and control and demonstrates strong potential for broader applications in diverse object recognition and detection scenarios.

title: SLPT-Net: A spatiotemporal learning framework for automated sow contraction recognition and farrowing time prediction
abstract: The frequency of sow contraction behavior is a key physiological indicator of imminent parturition, and accurate farrowing time estimation is crucial for improving piglet survival rates. However, existing behavior recognition methods — mainly adapted from human action analysis — often face limitations in generalization and computational efficiency when applied in real farm environments. To address these challenges, this study proposes a two-stage recognition and prediction framework named sparse lightweight perception and transformer-based network for sow contraction recognition and farrowing time prediction (SLPT-Net), which integrates contraction behavior recognition and farrowing time prediction. In the first stage, a lightweight 3D convolutional sub-network called sparse lightweight perception network for 3D video-based sow contraction behavior recognition (SLP3D) is developed to identify contraction behaviors. It incorporates a lightweight spatial channel attention (LSCA) module, a partial bidirectional feature pyramid network (PBFPN), and the Swish activation function to enhance spatiotemporal feature representation while reducing computational overhead. In the second stage, a Transformer-based classifier utilizes sequences of contraction behaviors to estimate the farrowing stage, followed by a post-processing algorithm to predict the actual farrowing time. A video dataset of sow contraction behaviors was constructed for evaluation. Experimental results show that SLP3D achieves a mean accuracy of 96.40% at 65.66 FPS, outperforming mainstream methods in both accuracy and real-time performance. The farrowing time prediction model yields an average error of 1.17 h, demonstrating the framework’s effectiveness. This work presents a novel, efficient solution for intelligent monitoring of sow farrowing behavior, with strong potential for practical application in smart farming systems.

title: Optimized ensemble learning frameworks for early grain yield prediction in winter wheat using static and multitemporal multispectral UAV data
abstract: A stacked ensemble learning framework was developed leveraging the large-scale spatial and temporal diversity in a winter wheat breeding program. Multispectral data were collected from 1098 plots comprising 586 genetically diverse advanced breeding lines at tillering, stem elongation, reproductive, early grain filling, mid grain filling, and late dough stages. Raw spectral information, 28 vegetation indices and 16 grey-level co-occurrence matrices were used– both individually and in combination –to train five machine learning algorithms– elastic net , support vector regression , k-nearest neighbours , random forest , and extreme gradient boosting . Static and temporal models were trained for spatial interpolation and genetic extrapolation, followed by internal and external validation. Multispectral features showed stage-specific discriminatory power for separating yield groups, peaking between the reproductive and mid grain filling stages. Classification was limited by overlap between medium- and high-yielding groups. Models integrating multispectral data across growth stages outperformed all other strategies. Elastic net performed best overall, while support vector regression showed the most consistent ranking. Base learners achieved average prediction accuracy of 55.85 % and 46.00 %, with AUC values of 0.73 and 0.66 for internal and external validation, respectively. Selected base-learners were used for stacked elastic net ensemble learning, which increased overall prediction (∼18 %) and classification (∼7 %) accuracies, while reducing errors (∼10 %). These improvements were primarily attributed to reduced bias. Overall, this study presents a scalable machine learning framework trained and validated on an operational breeding program for data-driven UAV-assisted early generation selection, providing a methodological reference for future research and deployment.

title: Fusion of keypoint detection and posture-aware correction for body measurement of dairy cattle
abstract: Accurate and efficient non-contact body measurement of dairy cattle is essential for Precision Livestock Farming (PLF), enabling data-driven monitoring, management, and genetic improvement. Keypoint-based computer vision methods offer a powerful approach to this task. However, two critical challenges hinder its effective implementation: (1) Inaccurate localization of keypoints caused by weak visual features, and (2) Measurement deviations induced by non-standard postures. To address these issues, a novel method named CowSizeNet was proposed, which integrates keypoint detection, initial size estimation, and posture-aware correction into a coherent process. In the first stage, the Cattle Keypoint Detection Network (CKDNet) was developed to achieve reliable keypoint localization. Two dedicated modules introduced in this study, the Bidirectional Feature Enhancement Module (BFEM) and the Hyper-Graph Association Enhancement Module (HGAEM), were incorporated to enrich visual representations and strengthen spatial associations, significantly improving the localization accuracy of visually ambiguous regions. In the second stage, stereo image disparity and camera parameters were utilized to obtain depth information, enabling 3D projection of detected keypoints and initial body size estimation. In the final stage, a Posture-aware Correction Graph Convolutional Network (PC-GCN) was introduced to learn the nonlinear relationships among keypoint geometry, joint angles, and body measurement deviations under varying postures. By regressing and compensating posture-related deviations, the model yielded more accurate and consistent body size estimations. Experiments verified the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed method. For Body Length (BL), Body Height (BH), and Hip Height (HH), the Mean Absolute Percentage Errors (MAPE) were 4.26%, 1.97%, and 2.19%, respectively, satisfying the accuracy requirements for automated body measurement in PLF. Furthermore, the design and development of supporting terminal devices and visualization platforms further enhanced the practical value of the proposed method, promoting its use in dairy farm management.

title: Unified vision: Multi-task learning for retinal image-based cattle trait classification
abstract: Reliable identification of demographic traits such as gender, breed, and age is fundamental to automated herd management in precision livestock farming. Traditional approaches based on external morphology or manual tagging are often labour-intensive, error-prone, or susceptible to tampering. In contrast, retinal imaging provides a non-invasive and stable biometric modality with high inter-individual variability. This study proposes a multi-task learning (MTL) framework for simultaneous classification of gender, breed, and age group from cattle retinal fundus images. The architecture incorporates multi-scale spatial feature fusion to capture fine-grained vascular patterns and broader retinal structures, positional encoding combined with Transformer-based relational modeling to enhance spatial dependency learning, and uncertainty-weighted multi-task optimization to balance task contributions adaptively. Experiments were conducted on a dataset of 1,206 retinal images from 233 individual cattle, annotated with demographic labels. The proposed model achieved strong performance across all three tasks. For gender classification, it attained 0.909 in accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Breed classification yielded scores of 0.880, 0.886, 0.880, and 0.883, while age classification achieved 0.926, 0.929, 0.926, and 0.927, respectively. Visualization analyses using t-SNE demonstrated that the multi-task framework produced more compact intra-class clustering and greater inter-class separability compared to single-task baselines. Grad-CAM visualizations further confirmed that the proposed model consistently focused on anatomically meaningful regions, particularly the optic disc and major vascular bifurcations. Comparative analysis confirmed the superiority of integrating multi-scale feature extraction, spatial relational modeling, and task uncertainty weighting in retinal image-based livestock phenotyping. This work highlights the potential of retinal imaging combined with multi-task learning for developing scalable, interpretable, and automated livestock phenotyping systems.

title: A method for quantifying feeding behavior of grass carp in outdoor ponds with complex backgrounds
abstract: In aquaculture, precise quantification of fish feeding behavior is essential for formulating feeding strategies. However, dynamic background factors in outdoor pond farming can interfere with the extraction of fish school behavior characteristics. To address this, a novel method has been proposed for quantifying fish behavior under complex conditions. First, the MusFormer model was developed, integrating a mixed transformer encoder with a custom multi-scale feature fusion decoder. This decoder includes a residual MLP and a multi-scale feature fusion module, enabling the generation of high-precision semantic segmentation images of fish school feeding areas. Subsequently, a new method called QFA (Quantitative Feeding Activity Index) was established to quantify the spatial characteristics of fish school feeding behavior. By assigning weights to pixel points, this method reduces interference from segmentation errors and dynamic changes in the background mask. Finally, to evaluate its effectiveness under complex background conditions, the QFA framework was integrated with three mainstream temporal classification models: RNN, Transformer, and RCNN. This combination yielded classification accuracies of 90.97 %, 88.73 %, and 91.86 %, respectively, outperforming existing fish appetite assessment methods, which achieve a maximum accuracy of 84.17 %. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for quantifying fish feeding behavior in outdoor ponds with typical complex background disturbances.

title: Supervised contrastive regression learning for predicting soluble solids content of blueberries using hyperspectral imaging
abstract: Hyperspectral imaging technology enables rapid and non-destructive assessment of fruits. However, acquiring a large-scale and well-balanced labeled dataset remains a significant challenge, primarily due to destructive reference measurements and difficulty sourcing samples that cover a wide and balanced distribution of quality attributes, which exacerbates overfitting risk when sample diversity is limited. Additionally, most deep learning methods optimize using mean squared error and regularization losses without explicitly learning feature representations relevant to regression tasks, making it difficult to learn robust, continuous feature representations. To address these challenges, we propose a spectral quantitative regression framework with supervised contrastive learning (SQR-SCL). A C-Mixup method selects sample pairs based on target-value similarity and interpolates their features and target values, enhancing sample diversity. A differential preservation and continuity feature learning (DPCFL) module learns continuous feature representations while preserving differences between samples. The DPCFL module draws samples with similar target values closer together and pushes those with differing values further apart, sorting features in the embedding space by target value. Such ordering prevents the model from making significantly different predictions for similar inputs, thereby improving prediction stability. A projection head in the DPCFL module ensures that extracted features preserve inter-sample differences and enhances their discriminative power. In this study, reflectance hyperspectral images and soluble solids content (SSC, ∘Bx) were acquired for 1010 blueberries in five sample groups. On this dataset, SQR-SCL achieved a test R2 of 0.884 and an RMSEP of 0.641(∘Bx), outperforming compared deep learning and traditional methods.

title: TP-Duck: A cage-reared duck behavior recognition model with lightweight interaction mechanism and text prompts
abstract: Accurate and automated behavior recognition is critical for welfare assessment and production management in intensive duck farming. However, cage-reared duck behavior recognition remains challenging due to the high visual similarity among behaviors and the tendency for subtle discriminative motion cues to be misinterpreted by the duck’s dominant body appearance under cage interference. To address these challenges, this study proposes a lightweight vision–language model with partial-star operation and text prompts for cage-reared duck behavior recognition (TP-Duck). Specifically, a Lightweight Partial-Star Operation Block (LPS) is designed to efficiently capture fine-grained discriminative features through partial convolution for channel-sparse computation and star operation for high-dimensional non-linear feature excitation. Building upon LPS, a Text-Prompted LPS Block (TP-LPS) is further developed to leverage pre-trained vision–language embeddings for cross-modal feature modulation, thereby enhancing the model’s capacity to disambiguate behaviors with similar postures in complex cage environments. Extensive experiments were conducted on a self-built cage-reared duck behavior dataset. TP-Duck achieves an F1 score of 89.4%, surpassing the baseline YOLOv11s and state-of-the-art YOLO26s by 2.2 and 5.0 percentage points, respectively, while reducing parameters by 0.64 M and 1.18 M. The results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves superior recognition accuracy with reduced model complexity, providing an effective solution for automated duck behavior monitoring in intensive farming systems.

title: PA-SWE: a posture-aware sow weight estimation framework via skeleton-calibrated multimodal fusion
abstract: Accurate body weight monitoring of gestating sows is critical for precision feeding and reproductive performance optimization. While deep learning has shown promise in image-based weight estimation, existing RGB-based methods are sensitive to posture variation, and depth-based alternatives incur higher deployment costs and environmental constraints. This study introduces Posture-Aware Sow Weight Estimation (PA-SWE), a posture‑aware RGB–skeletal framework that uses posture as an auxiliary source of structural information rather than treating it as nuisance variation. The framework comprises an upstream module that simultaneously outputs instance segmentation masks and anatomical keypoints from the top‑view RGB images, and a downstream module that fuses RGB appearance features with a skeletal graph via compact bilinear pooling to jointly predict body weight and posture. Evaluation on a commercial farm dataset containing 48 gestating sows of a single breed follows an event‑level protocol: image‑level predictions within each weighing event are aggregated using the median to produce the final event-level estimate. PA‑SWE achieves an event‑level mean absolute error of 2.814 kg, a root mean square error of 3.513 kg, and an R2 of 0.975, together with a macro‑averaged F1‑score of 92.89% for three‑class posture classification. Pig‑level statistical analyses further showed that the error reduction relative to RGB‑only baselines is significant and consistent across individuals. These results suggest that explicit integration of skeletal cues can reduce posture‑related estimation errors and improve event‑level weight estimation in the current farm‑specific setting. The proposed framework therefore offers a practical option for contactless monitoring of gestating sows without requiring strict standing-posture standardization under crate-based monitoring conditions.

title: SDrAwberry: Scale-referenced Depth-Anything-3 long-sequence reconstruction for Strawberry canopy volume estimation
abstract: Canopy volume is a key structural trait for crop monitoring and phenotyping platforms, but reliable plant-level canopy volume estimation in commercial strawberry fields remains challenging due to repetitive canopy structure, limited texture on bed surfaces, and the need to process long, nearly linear image sequences without loop closure. This paper presents SDrAwberry, a scale-referenced long-sequence 3D reconstruction and plant-level canopy volume estimation pipeline using synchronized tri-view RGB images collected by a ground robot across eight strawberry plant beds on one representative field acquisition date. The proposed pipeline enables a memory-efficient processing of long sequence data by partitioning the data into overlapping batches, fusing the partitioned batches into a global reconstruction in the form of point cloud, and estimating plant canopy volume by segmenting individual plants, mesh reconstruction, and scale calibration with reference boxes. The pipeline was validated by comparing the number of segmented plants and manual plant counts, and by evaluating metric scale recovery with reference-box volume self-validation. The instance extraction stage showed strong agreement with manual plant counts, with a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 5.36 %. Reference-box self-validation also indicated consistent metric scale recovery, with an MAPE of 3.95 %. Direct plant-level canopy-volume ground truth was not available, so plant-volume outputs were interpreted as scale-referenced reconstructed traits rather than direct volume-accuracy validation. These results indicate that feed-forward multi-view geometry transformers can be extended to field-scale, metrically meaningful phenotyping via batching-and-fusion and scale-referenced volumetric reconstruction. Code and data are available at: https://github.com/Sycamorers/SDrAwberry.

title: Toward optimal sampling rate selection and unbiased classification for precise activity recognition of farm quadruped animals
abstract: With the rapid advancements in deep learning techniques, wearable sensor-aided animal activity recognition (AAR) has demonstrated promising performance, thereby improving livestock management efficiency as well as animal health and welfare monitoring. However, existing research often prioritizes overall performance, overlooking the fact that classification accuracies for specific animal behavioral categories may remain unsatisfactory. This issue typically stems from suboptimal sampling rates or class imbalance problems. To address these challenges and achieve high classification accuracy across all individual behaviors in farm quadruped animals, we propose a novel Individual-Behavior-Aware Network (IBA-Net). This network enhances the recognition of each specific behavior by simultaneously customizing features and calibrating the classifier. Specifically, considering that different behaviors require varying sampling rates to achieve optimal performance, we design a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE)-based Feature Customization (MFC) module. This module adaptively fuses data from multiple sampling rates, capturing customized features tailored to various animal behaviors. Additionally, to mitigate classifier bias toward majority classes caused by class imbalance, we develop a Neural Collapse-driven Classifier Calibration (NC3) module. This module introduces a fixed equiangular tight frame (ETF) classifier during the classification stage, maximizing the angles between pair-wise classifier vectors and thereby improving the classification performance for minority classes. To validate the effectiveness of IBA-Net, we conduct experiments on three public datasets for goat, cattle, and horse activity recognition. The results demonstrate that our method exhibits strong and competitive performance across all three datasets compared to existing approaches. Specifically, it achieves the highest values across three datasets: for goat, 93.17 % accuracy, 87.17 % F1-score, and 91.71 % recall; for cattle, 91.42 % accuracy, 90.62 % F1-score, 88.06 % precision, and 93.64 % recall; and for horse, 84.34 % F1-score and 84.05 % precision. Notably, the recall values exhibit substantial enhancements, surpassing the baseline method by 16.98 %, 15.78 %, and 4.91 % on the goat, cattle, and horse datasets, respectively. These improvements are particularly evident for the minority classes, while high recognition performance is maintained for the majority classes. These results confirm that IBA-Net effectively enhances classification accuracy across all animal behavioral categories, while aligning with the initial goal of achieving high recall values and maximizing overall classification performance.

title: Autonomous crop and weed detection in multiple agricultural fields using YOLO-based models with combined real and synthesized images
abstract: Accurate crop and weed detection is critical for targeted weed control, particularly for weeds in intra-row areas. Site-specific weeding where weeds appear can reduce herbicide use and labor costs. However, field variability, including crop growth stage, soil texture, illumination, and camera viewpoint, remains challenging. This study presents a practical data-construction workflow that integrates synthetically generated images with labeled real images to train crop-weed detection models. You Only Look Once (YOLO) versions 4 and 8, convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures, were evaluated because of their detection performance and computational efficiency. Training YOLOv8 with a mixed synthetic-real dataset derived from four crop types collected across agricultural fields in four Japanese prefectures improved detection of 11 crop and weed classes. On the validation data, the model achieved a precision of 0.92, a recall of 0.89, an F1-score of 0.90, and a mean average precision (mAP50) of 0.92. On independent real test images, the proposed YOLOv8 model achieved a mAP50 of 0.88, with class-level Recall50 values ranging from 0.67 to 0.97 and a mean Recall50 of 0.85. These results show that synthetic images are useful for reducing annotation effort and improving class balance when combined with real field images, but they do not replace independent real-image validation. The method therefore provides a promising perception component for future intra-row weeding systems, while robot-level testing, embedded inference, and actuation accuracy remain necessary before autonomous deployment.

title: MoeBi-ViT: Non-destructive shoot-stage phenotyping of lettuce in plant factory via dual-branch mixture-of-experts network and enhanced segmentation
abstract: In plant factories, increased crop yield often comes at the price of higher energy inputs. Understanding the relationship between environmental regulation and crop growth helps maximize energy use efficiency. Thus, dynamic monitoring of crop biomass is critical for optimizing crop management practices. The morphological parameters (canopy length and width, plant height, leaf area) and biomass indicators (fresh weight and dry weight) jointly form the key metrics for evaluating crop growth and development. However, traditional manual measurement methods are typically inefficient, costly, labor-intensive, and time-consuming. This study proposed a rapid, non-destructive lettuce biomass estimation method based on two-stage multi-modal deep learning: firstly, a gated attention-enhanced segmentation model—Mambaout-Mask2Former (MOMF)—was adopted to address background interference in lettuce phenotypic estimation, which reduces parameter count and model complexity while enabling accurate lettuce mask extraction and background elimination; secondly, a dual-branch Mixture-of-Experts regression network (MoeBi-ViT) was constructed to lower the computational complexity of the biomass regression network while ensuring generalization across scenarios, which was achieved via the combination of a Transformer-based Mixture-of-Experts encoder (TEME) and bi-attentional feature fusion (BAF). MoeBi-ViT activates only ∼ 37 % of weights per inference (compared to fully parameter-activated models) while maintaining precise biomass regression performance. Experimental results have shown that MoeBi-ViT outperformed the baseline Vision Transformer (ViT) significantly in lettuce biomass estimation with only a marginal increase in inference parameters, achieving a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.936 for fresh weight prediction and a 12.3 % overall improvement in the aggregated R2 metric. Ablation studies confirmed the effectiveness of TEME and BAF. To explain the model’s operating mechanism, activation frequencies were counted to analyze the contribution of different expert types in the final Mixture-of-Experts layer to various phenotypic parameters. Additionally, the trained model was applied to an unlabeled lettuce dataset to verify its accuracy in continuous growth monitoring.
