First, multiple quality indicators, including soluble solids content (SSC), pH, and firmness, were integrated, and a ripeness quantification and classification model was established using the weighted k-means clustering algorithm, providing an efficient method for rapid field grading. Second, to overcome the difficulty of acquiring in-situ field samples, we employed theWasserstein Generative Adversarial Network with Gradient Penalty (WGAN-GP) to generate synthetic hyperspectral data labeled with ripeness, thereby enhancing the diversity and richness of the training dataset. Finally, we designed the multi-scale attention residual network (MSA-ResNet) ripeness perception modelto fully exploit the interrelationships among multiple indicators. Through feature learning and key band selection, the model achieves ripeness grading using only four key spectral bands. Experimental results demonstrated that the proposed MSA-ResNet model achieved a classification accuracy of 87.10% on the field test set under a single split, with a mean accuracy of 83.87% ± 3.23% across five repeated random splits. This study provides a feasible method for in-situ ripeness detection and offers a reference for ripeness discrimination in harvesting robots.

title: Full-season wheat phenotyping using UAV-based multi-source remote sensing: dynamic time-series modeling and high-throughput trait extraction
abstract: High-throughput and full-season phenotypic characterization of wheat is essential for crop breeding and precision agriculture. However, the automated extraction of plot-level traits from unmanned aerial vehicle(UAV)-based multi-source data remains challenging because of complex field backgrounds, inconsistent spatial representations among data modalities, and temporal variation in canopy structure. This study developed an automated framework for full-season wheat phenotyping using UAV-acquired RGB, multispectral, thermal infrared, and three-dimensional(3D)point cloud data. The framework focused on three key tasks: plot-level wheat segmentation from 3D point clouds, spatial integration between 3D point clouds and two-dimensional(2D)imagery, and dynamic analysis of phenotypic traits across growth stages. A 3D wheat point cloud segmentation model, termed 3D Wheat Point-Transformer(3D Wheat PT), was developed to separate wheat plots from background points under different cultivation patterns. Based on the segmented point clouds, projection and feature-matching strategies were used to generate spatially consistent plot masks for 2D multi-source imagery, enabling integrated trait extraction from both 2D and 3D data. In addition, the WheatMorph software system was developed to support visualization, automated segmentation, and quantitative extraction of wheat phenotypic traits, forming an end-to-end workflow from data input to result output. Phenotypic traits extracted from 15 sampling stages were further used to construct dynamic temporal curves for growth stage identification, cultivar classification, and trait prediction. Experimental results showed that the proposed 3D Wheat PT achieved segmentation accuracies of 94.4%, 91.8%, and 92.5% across three experimental sites and cultivation patterns. The extracted canopy height showed strong agreement with measured values(R2 = 0.943). Using canopy height growth-rate dynamics as input features, the Long Short-Term Memory model achieved the highest prediction accuracy of 76.7% at the jointing stage(127 days after sowing). These results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides an effective and scalable solution for automated multi-source wheat phenotyping and temporal trait analysis throughout the growing season.

title: Accurate prediction of wheat grain protein content via integration of genomic prediction and high-throughput phenotyping in breeding fields
abstract: Grain protein content (GPC) is a critical determinant of baking quality, and its accurate prediction is essential for breeders, decision-makers, and the agricultural industry. Currently, GPC prediction primarily relies on genomics and phenomics. However, the integration of high-throughput phenotypic (HTP) and genotypic data to predict GPC remains underexplored. In this study, a novel approach was proposed, termed phenotypic genomic prediction (PGP), which combines genomic prediction (GP) and phenotypic prediction (PP) using machine learning (ML) to enhance GPC predictive performance. The predictive performance of the PGP method was evaluated using a population of 262 wheat recombinant inbred lines (RILs) under full irrigation (FI) and limited irrigation (LI) conditions. First, the correlations between GPC and 29 traits across four developmental stages including anthesis, early grain-filling, middle grain-filling, and late grain-filling were analyzed in both environments. The results showed that the middle grain-filling stage had the highest correlation under FI conditions, whereas the early grain-filling stage exhibited the strongest correlation under LI conditions. In addition, the correlations under LI conditions were higher than those under FI conditions. Subsequently, eight commonly used ML methods were separately applied to predict GPC using GP and PP datasets. The optimal GP and PP datasets were then selected, combined in pairs to generate nine PGP datasets, and further evaluated using seven ML methods to identify the best performing model. The combination of rrBLUP_GP & RR_PP based on the GB method was identified as the optimal model (FI, 0.60; LI, 0.69). Compared to GP (FI, 0.41; LI, 0.39), PP (FI, 0.43; LI, 0.56) demonstrated superior prediction accuracy. On average, the predictive performance of PGP was 31.10 % and 15.13 % higher than that of GP and PP, respectively. Feature importance analysis of the PGP models under both environmental conditions showed that the relative importance of GP (FI: 54.13 %; LI: 30.41 %) and PP (FI: 45.87 %; LI: 69.59 %) differed across environments, and both contributed positively to the final prediction outcomes. This approach effectively captures the complex relationships between genotypes, HTP, and GPC traits. Overall, the proposed PGP method demonstrates effective GPC prediction capabilities and can be extended to other traits and crops.

title: A physical-context-conditioned multimodal fusion network for estimating maize canopy nitrogen content using multi-source UAV remote sensing data
abstract: Maize canopy nitrogen content (CNC) is a key indicator of crop nitrogen nutritional status. However, under complex field conditions, single-spectral models are susceptible to spectral saturation and environmental heterogeneity, limiting their estimation accuracy and generalization. Many multimodal approaches use concatenation, fixed weighting, or attention across parallel modality streams, but heterogeneous modalities are commonly treated as parallel predictors, failing to leverage observations from heterogeneous modalities to condition spectral representation learning and regulate branch-level contributions. To address this limitation, this study proposes a Physical-Context-Conditioned Multimodal Neural Network (PCCMN) with an asymmetric, two-stage physical-context-conditioned fusion strategy for maize CNC estimation. Rather than treating hyperspectral, LiDAR, and thermal infrared observations as equivalent inputs, PCCMN treats hyperspectral features as the primary information source for CNC estimation, while canopy structure and thermal status are jointly encoded as sample-specific physical context. Instead of being directly concatenated with spectral features, this physical context is used as a query to selectively aggregate nitrogen-sensitive spectral tokens. An adaptive gating mechanism subsequently regulates the relative contributions of the context-conditioned spectral representation and the physical context representation. This study analyzed data from field experiments conducted in two consecutive years, 2024 and 2025. PCCMN consistently outperformed the comparative models, across the three growth stages and both year-specific held-out test sets, with mean R2 values of 0.79–0.85 and RMSE values of 0.17–0.65. Ablation experiments demonstrated that the performance gains arose from the coordinated effects of multimodal complementarity, context-conditioned spectral selection, and adaptive gating-based fusion rather than from simply adding auxiliary modalities. Gating analysis showed stronger weighting toward the context-conditioned spectral representation in the trumpet-stage model and more balanced allocation between the spectral and physical-context representations in the tasseling- and grain-filling-stage models. SHAP analysis further showed that model decisions were primarily associated with stage-dependent spectral responses concentrated in the red-edge region.These results demonstrate that organizing heterogeneous UAV observations according to their functional roles and dynamically regulating their information flow can support more consistent CNC estimation under phenological and interannual variability. PCCMN therefore provides a physical-context-conditioned multimodal framework for field-scale crop nitrogen monitoring.

title: Latent-space feature reconstruction-enhanced semantic segmentation for agricultural field roads under visual degradation
abstract: Visual perception for autonomous agricultural machinery on unstructured inter-field transfer roads is often affected by drastic illumination variations and dust contamination. These degradations reduce the robustness of segmentation models in real-world field-road environments. To address these challenges, we propose LDRSeg, a robust semantic segmentation framework that improves robustness under degradation conditions by reconstructing degraded features in the latent space. First, to expand degraded data under realistic acquisition constraints, a GAN-based degradation synthesis pipeline is constructed to generate multi-type degraded samples while preserving geometry and semantic consistency. Then, a feature reconstruction module guided by a pre-trained latent diffusion prior is introduced to perform implicit denoising and distribution bias correction in the intermediate feature stream, and a progressive decoupled training protocol is adopted to learn a robust mapping from degraded features to clean semantics. Experiments on real degraded test sets show that LDRSeg achieves 75.80 % mIoU and 84.41 % mAcc, outperforming the baseline by 3.17 % and 3.04 %, respectively. It also reduces the Relative Corruption Error (RCE) to 4.20 % for mIoU and 2.97 % for mAcc. In heavy-dust scenes, LDRSeg improves mIoU by 5.19 %. Beyond the primary architecture, cross-architecture experiments further show that the proposed module can improve degraded-scene robustness when integrated into the evaluated CNN- and Transformer-based segmentation architectures.

title: PineWilt-MultiSeg: Joint spatial–spectral learning enables precise detection of pine wilt disease
abstract: Pine wilt disease (PWD) poses a serious threat to pine forest ecosystems, highlighting the need for timely and accurate identification of affected trees to support targeted removal and epidemic control. UAV remote sensing combined with deep learning has shown considerable potential for individual-tree-level PWD monitoring. However, most existing studies rely on unimodal imagery, which may provide insufficient information for distinguishing diseased trees from complex forest backgrounds. Although RGB imagery captures detailed spatial, textural, and morphological features, multispectral imagery provides additional information on vegetation pigments, canopy water status, and physiological stress. Integrating these complementary information sources may therefore improve detection accuracy and model robustness. Nevertheless, publicly accessible benchmark datasets providing co-registered RGB and multispectral imagery with pixel-level annotations for PWD remain scarce, limiting systematic model development and comparison. To help address this gap, we constructed PineWilt-MultiSeg, a high-resolution multimodal benchmark dataset comprising 3938 spatially aligned pairs of RGB and 10-band multispectral images with pixel-level semantic annotations. The dataset covers pine trees at the middle and late stages of PWD under diverse canopy conditions and forest backgrounds. Five representative semantic segmentation architectures — SegFormer, PSPNet, Twins-PCPVT, DeepLabv3+, and EncNet — were evaluated to establish unimodal RGB and multispectral benchmarks, while the CMX architecture was employed to assess multimodal feature fusion. Experimental results indicate that multimodal fusion provides consistent and measurable performance gains over unimodal RGB and multispectral inputs, with mIoU improvements of 1.75% and 5.95%, respectively, demonstrating the effectiveness of joint spatial–spectral information integration. Additionally, the influence of spatial resolution on detection accuracy was investigated, and the physical spectral characteristics of diseased trees were analyzed, confirming the superiority of multimodal data in jointly leveraging spatial and spectral information. This study provides a solid data foundation and methodological reference for multimodal detection of pine wilt disease. The dataset and models will be made publicly available at: https://github.com/caudjcc/PineWilt-MultiSeg.git

title: SpecMCR: A multi-channel spectral regression framework with clustering and GAN-based augmentation for accurate grape sugar prediction
abstract: Accurate estimation of grape sugar content is essential for evaluating fruit maturity and wine quality, yet conventional spectral models often struggle with large variations caused by grape cultivars and environmental conditions. To overcome these challenges, we propose SpecMCR, a spectral multi-channel regression framework that combines unsupervised clustering, score-based conditional GAN (SCGAN) augmentation, and channel-wise regression. The clustering module partitions the spectra into three structurally stable channels, effectively reducing intra-class variability. SCGAN further refines these channels by generating high-quality spectra that enhance boundary regions. With these components, SpecMCR achieves an RMSE of 19.70 and an R2 of 0.85 on the test set while the RMSE values of PLS and SVM above 26, it also outperforms deep models including Inception-v1 and ResNet18, which show test RMSE values around 26.78 and 23.48 respectively. The results demonstrate that SpecMCR captures the heterogeneous structure of spectral data more effectively than single-channel and deep learning baselines, offering a robust and automated solution for agricultural spectroscopy.

title: Harvesting sequence optimization for clustered strawberries using a fruit-level harvesting difficulty score
abstract: Existing fruit-harvesting sequence planning mainly focuses on minimizing manipulator travel distance, while fruit-specific harvesting difficulty is rarely considered in clustered environments. This study proposed a difficulty-aware harvesting-sequence optimization framework integrating fruit-level harvesting difficulty score (HDS) prediction, dynamic HDS updating, and weighted-sum multi-criteria sequence planning. A two-stage convolutional neural network (CNN)-based vision framework was developed to estimate fruit-level HDS, and the harvesting sequence was re-optimized after each virtual fruit removal using genetic-algorithm-based (MOP-GA) and simulated-annealing-based (MOP-SA) solvers. The HDS regression model achieved an MAE of 6.55% and an R2 of 72.39%. In offline experiments, MOP-GA reduced the average HDS per fruit to 0.282, compared with 0.291 for TSP and 0.297 for bottom-up. Indoor robot experiments across nine strawberry-cluster scenes further showed lower HDS values for MOP-GA (0.197) and MOP-SA (0.204) than for TSP (0.235) and bottom-up (0.237), with all four proposed-versus-baseline comparisons remaining significant after Holm correction. MOP-GA also achieved a lower observed failure rate than TSP (19.11% vs. 26.67%), although the overall difference in failure probability among methods was not statistically significant. These results indicated that dynamically incorporating fruit-level harvesting difficulty can improve harvesting-sequence feasibility in clustered environments, while the increased computational cost remained a limitation for real-time deployment.

title: UAV remote sensing monitoring of tea heat-drought stress in complex tea garden environments
abstract: The monitoring of tea heat–drought stress (THS) via UAV remote sensing involves challenges such as complex plantation environments, strong variations in illumination and shadow, the small scale of the diseased spots, and weak spectral differences between THS spots and healthy areas. To address these issues, this study proposes a UAV remote sensing monitoring method for THS in complex tea plantation environments. A scheme called Multispectral Tea Heat-Drought Stress Detection Network (MS-THSNet) is designed, in which a dual-branch feature extraction backbone is employed to exploit the complementary advantages of different modalities in terms of capturing texture information and spectral characteristics. To further enhance the cross-modal feature integration, a Modality Interaction Transformer Module (MITM) and an Adaptive Multispectral Fusion Network structure (AMF-Net) are introduced. The MITM models the global dependency relationships among different spectral bands through a cross-spectral feature interaction mechanism, enabling complementary enhancement of multispectral features and alleviating the insufficient discriminative representation caused by uneven illumination, shadow, and the weak spectral differences of THS spots. The AMF-Net structure adaptively weights and integrates the fused features to emphasize spot-related characteristics while suppressing interference from complex backgrounds. MS-THSNet also includes a Context-Guided Attention Module (CGAM) to perform cross-channel and cross-spatial contextual attention modeling on the fused features, thereby improving the localization and recognition accuracy of THS spots at different scales. In addition, a lightweight small-object detection head is adopted to enhance the perception of tiny THS spots. Experimental results indicate that the proposed method achieves a precision of 86.4%, a recall of 80.5%, and a mean average precision (mAP) of 87.8%, significantly outperforming other state-of-the-art methods. Compared with mainstream multimodal detection methods, the proposed method has an mAP that is improved by more than 3.5%, with a 7% improvement over the baseline detection network, thus validating its effectiveness for UAV monitoring of THS in complex tea garden environments.

title: MCAFNet: A multimodal audio-visual cross-attention fusion network for on-the-branch durian (Durio zibethinus L.) fruit maturity assessment
abstract: Accurate on-the-branch durian maturity assessment is essential for determining appropriate harvest timing, yet conventional experience-based evaluation is operator-dependent, and existing automated approaches have limited applicability in complex orchard environments. This study proposes a Multimodal Cross-Attention Fusion Network (MCAFNet) that integrates fruit images, stem images, and fruit-knocking acoustic signals for in-field durian maturity classification. An improved lightweight detector, SG-YOLO, extracts fruit and stem regions, while Mel spectrogram, mel-frequency cepstral coefficient (MFCC), and Chroma representations are stacked into a three-channel acoustic feature map. A Transformer-based cross-attention module subsequently fuses modality-specific features to exploit complementary maturity information. Under five-fold cross-validation, MCAFNet achieved an accuracy of 86.27 % ± 2.32 % and a macro_F1-score of 85.63 % ± 2.55 %, outperforming all 11 evaluated alternative multimodal fusion methods. Compared with the strongest competing method, FDFR-Net, accuracy and macro_F1-score increased by 2.15 and 2.22 percentage points, respectively. Moreover, integrating extracted fruit and stem regions with acoustic information improved accuracy by 6.07 percentage points and macro_F1-score by 5.48 percentage points relative to a full-image-plus-audio strategy. Ablation analyses indicated that fruit images provided the strongest discriminative information, while stem images and acoustic signals contributed complementary maturity cues. A user-oriented application was also developed to support practical assessment. These findings highlight the potential of region-focused visual-acoustic fusion for on-the-branch durian maturity classification and provide a foundation for intelligent harvesting systems.

title: Species-Conditioned hierarchical decoding and cross-attention for uncertainty-aware veterinary skin disease recognition
abstract: Veterinary dermatology is facing two diagnostic challenges. First, many conditions show overlapping visual signs such as alopecia, erythema, crusting, scaling, nodules, and plaques, making image-based recognition difficult. Second, the same visual pattern may correspond to different diseases in cats, cattle, and dogs, which makes flat disease classification unreliable when host species is ignored. While deep learning has advanced animal health monitoring, existing systems are often limited to single species or binary detection tasks. To address this, we propose a species-conditioned deep learning framework designed to analyze standard RGB images across diverse hosts. Our approach introduces a novel architecture featuring: (1) an EfficientNetV2-S backbone for feature extraction; (2) a dedicated pathway for host-species representation; (3) disease-token construction with species-conditioned spatial-token modulation; and (4) species-gated cross-attention for disease classification. Furthermore, we incorporate uncertainty-aware analysis via MC-Dropout, conformal prediction, and Grad-CAM to ensure decision reliability. Evaluated on an internal dataset of 16,942 images (21 categories), the proposed Unified SGCA model achieved 97.5 % disease accuracy and 98.0 % macro-F1 on the internal test set, while SGCA Cross-Attention achieved 96.9 % accuracy and 97.4 % macro-F1. Crucially, on a heterogeneous external cohort of 1,351 internet-derived images characterized by varying quality and background complexity, the model maintained robust performance with a top-3 accuracy of 93.0 % for Unified SGCA and 88.8 % for SGCA Cross-Attention. This framework offers a scalable solution for veterinary decision support, farmer education, and zoonotic disease surveillance.

title: Machine learning-based analysis of electrical impedance spectroscopy for predicting plant gravimetric dynamics
abstract: Sensor-driven field monitoring in precision agriculture requires innovative solutions for real-time plant assessment. This study introduces a novel four-point impedance spectroscopy technique integrated with machine learning algorithms to evaluate plant physiological status under field conditions. A dual experimental setup, combining a gravimetric system with a custom electrical impedance module, enabled synchronized data acquisition. The proposed machine learning ensemble achieves a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.855 in predicting plant gravimetric dynamics, thus, outperforming conventional models and reducing error significantly. These findings support the advancement of impedance-based analytics as a scalable, non-invasive approach for large-scale agricultural monitoring.

title: Kernel loss prediction and parameter optimization for seed-maize husking devices using MFBD-DEM and Bi-level BO-ISSA-BP
abstract: The seed industry is a strategic pillar of food security, and kernel damage and loss during the mechanized harvesting of seed maize severely constrain improvements in seed quality. To address the problems of insufficient modeling accuracy of maize ears, limited predictive capability of traditional optimization methods, and the high kernel detachment and damage rates observed during the husking process, this study constructs a bract–kernel–cob flexible composite model for seed maize based on the Discrete Element Method (DEM), and employs Multi-Flexible-Body Dynamics–Discrete Element Method (MFBD–DEM) coupled simulation to reproduce the husking process. On this basis, the effects of surface-pattern arrangement, rotational speed, and inter-roller gap on kernel-loss behavior are systematically analyzed. Furthermore, a bi-level optimized BP neural network model (BO-ISSA-BP), combining Bayesian Optimization (BO) and an Improved Sparrow Search Algorithm (ISSA), is proposed to achieve high-precision prediction and optimization of key kernel-loss indices. Compared with the conventional SSA-BP model, the BO-ISSA-BP model reduces RMSE, MAPE, and MAE by 7.42%, 15.37%, and 14.91%, respectively, with the coefficient of determination R2 reaching 0.975. In comparison with the BO-BP model, more substantial improvements are observed across all error metrics. Under the optimal parameter combination, the bench test yields a detached-kernel loss rate and a damaged-kernel rate of 1.613% and 0.369%, respectively; the relative errors with respect to the theoretical optimum are 8.47% and 6.65%, and those relative to the model predictions are 7.09% and 6.35%, confirming the reliability and feasibility of the proposed prediction model and optimization method under practical operating conditions. The research findings not only provide a reliable theoretical basis for parameter optimization and performance prediction of seed-maize husking devices in China, but also offer a methodological framework for flexible body modeling and multi-objective optimization in agricultural machinery design.

title: Automated scanning framework for High-Fidelity 3D reconstruction and phenotypic analysis of rowed plug seedlings via 2D Gaussian Splatting
abstract: High-fidelity three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction enables the fine-grained phenotypic analysis and the establishment of digital twins of the pepper plug tray seedlings. Rowed seedlings in trays with tight interval poses significant challenge to multi-view 3D reconstruction. Previous investigations were largely restricted to the reconstruction of individual seedlings or the estimation of large-scale phenotypic traits of populations. In this study, a prototype with a multi-camera array was proposed to rapidly collect multiview dataset of pepper plug seedlings via row-scanning imaging. 2D Gaussian Splatting (2DGS), a cutting-edge 3D reconstruction approach based on novel view synthesis (NVS), was introduced to extract geometrically accurate mesh of pepper plug tray seedlings. In comparison to other multi-view 3D reconstruction methods, 2DGS yielded high-fidelity meshes with superior overall performance, achieving a competitive average chamfer distance error below 0.88 mm. Incorporated with PlantNet, a deep learning network for plant point cloud segmentation, sections of meshes were smoothly segmented and reassembled into independent seedling instances, providing reliable prerequisites of organ-level trait measurement. The proposed solution yielded the mean absolute percentage errors (MAPEs) of 0.91%, 2.67%, 3.88%, 4.95% in prediction of seedling height, main stem length, leaf blade length and leaf blade area, respectively. This study verified the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed row-scanning solution on pepper seedlings, promoting the development of high-throughput phenotyping equipment for plug tray seedlings in production.

title: Event triggered disturbance observer based nonlinear MPC for agricultural machinery trajectory tracking control
abstract: Autonomous operation of agricultural machinery in uneven and slippery terrain necessitates highly accurate trajectory tracking control. While Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) provides a robust formulation for this task, its real-time implementation is often limited by high computational demands, model uncertainties, and time-varying external disturbances. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel event-triggered disturbance observer based NMPC framework for agricultural machinery trajectory tracking to enhance tracking performance while reducing computational time. A nonlinear disturbance observer integrated with an Actor–Critic Neural Network (ACNN) is developed to dynamically estimate and compensate for both model uncertainties and time-varying external disturbances. A novel Pseudo-Huber cost function is utilized to formulate a dynamically smooth input saturation model to manage actuator constraints and prevent saturation-induced instability. To further reduce computational overhead, an event-triggered mechanism is implemented, where optimization updates are activated only when the prediction error between the system’s optimal forecasted state and its actual measured state exceeds a predefined threshold. This mechanism reduces the frequency of optimization computations, thereby alleviating the computational burden inherent in conventional NMPC, without compromising control performance. Comprehensive simulations are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme. The results demonstrate that the event-triggered disturbance observer based NMPC method not only achieves substantial savings in computational resources compared to NMPC but also maintains high trajectory tracking accuracy under the influence of disturbances.

title: Energy-Efficient path tracking control for autonomous tractors equipped with Hydro-Mechanical continuously variable transmission based on coordinated control methods
abstract: Autonomous tractors often prioritize tracking performance at the expense of operational energy consumption, negatively affecting their economic efficiency. To address this issue, this study proposes a coordinated control method that considers both tracking accuracy and fuel economy. First, a model predictive control algorithm is used to design the path tracking system, where longitudinal and lateral errors as tracking objectives, while acceleration and front wheel steering angular velocity as constraints. Then, a plowing resistance prediction model for tractors is developed using Long Short-Term Memory neural networks based on historical tractor plowing resistance data. Next, a dual-variable economic control strategy is developed to minimize the engine fuel consumption rate and optimize the hydraulic-mechanical continuously variable transmission efficiency ratio. The predicted working speed from the path tracking system and the predicted plowing resistance from the resistance prediction model are then passed to the economic control strategy, forming a coordinated control method that integrates tracking accuracy with fuel economy. We used pure pursuit and Stanley, both with a single-variable fuel-economy control strategy, as baselines. The proposed strategy’s effectiveness is validated through simulations and hardware-in-the-loop experiments. The results show that, compared with the alternative method, the proposed approach effectively reduces path tracking error and improves economic efficiency. Compared with the first and second comparison methods, the proposed approach reduces the standard deviation of speed variance by 70.27% for both methods, decreases longitudinal tracking error by 57.14% and 33.33%, respectively, reduces lateral tracking error by 33.33% and 55.56%, respectively, and lowers fuel consumption by 28.49% for both methods. This study provides valuable insights for improving both path tracking performance and energy efficiency in autonomous tractors.

title: Weather-based prediction of black locust (Robinia pseudoacacia L.) honey yield and quality: a reproducible computational system with operational deployment
abstract: Black locust (Robinia pseudoacacia L.; marketed as “acacia”) honey production in South Korea—accounting for over 70% of national honey output—has been increasingly affected by weather-driven disturbances, resulting in substantial production declines, notably in 2018 and 2020 ( Kim et al., 2022 ). Such episodes have been broadly attributed to impacts of climate change; however, a diagnostic framework identifying which weather variables, and at which phenological stages, drive the simultaneous decline in yield and quality has remained unavailable. Existing approaches rely either on uninterpretable machine-learning models that require large training data unavailable at the farm scale, or on single-variable rules-of-thumb that fail under multivariate weather conditions. Therefore, we present a reproducible computational system that addresses this gap through three integrated components: (i) two interpretable hierarchical weather indices—the Honey Harvest Weather Index (HHWI) for yield and the Honey Moisture Weather Index (HMWI) for moisture content—derived from five meteorological variables (maximum temperature, precipitation, relative humidity, wind speed, and solar radiation) across three phenological stages (bud formation, pre-flowering, and flowering); (ii) a generalized raster pipeline producing spatially-explicit predictions from gridded meteorological data; (iii) an operational forecast module generating real-time decision-support maps via inverse-distance interpolation. The system was validated using 570 farm-year records from 95 black locust apiaries (2020–2025) in South Korea and benchmarked against seven machine-learning alternatives. HHWI achieved a cross-validated R2 value of 0.395 (RMSE = 16.85 kg/colony) using three effective parameters and outperformed XGBoost in terms of cross-validated stability, exhibiting a 15-fold reduction in the overfitting gap. HMWI achieved a cross-validated R2 value of 0.668, with a moisture-grade classification accuracy of 96.0% (within ± 1 grade, Cohen’s κ = 0.41). This demonstrates its operational feasibility for weather-based quality prediction. Retrospective decomposition of the 2020 production minimum (18.4 kg/colony) indicated that approximately 60% of the deficit relative to the 2024 peak year (60.5 kg/colony) was attributable to maximum temperature during the pre-flowering stage. Cumulative temperature contributions across all phenological stages accounted for 80% of the deficit, transforming broad climate-change attribution into actionable diagnoses of specific weather variables and phenological stages. The data-driven breakpoints converged with published physiological thresholds for Apis mellifera , supporting the mechanistic interpretation. The complete system—including analysis script, raster pipeline, forecast module, and 22-checkpoint verification—was released as an open-source code, providing beekeepers and policymakers with a deployment-ready, weather-based decision-support system that requires only routine meteorological data. All codes and anonymized data are available on Zenodo ( https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20612458) .

title: Comparative analysis of machine learning models to restore gaps in multivariate time series leaf wetness sensor data
abstract: IoT (Internet of Things) has been utilized in agriculture in many ways. When collecting data from IoT-based sensors, errors can occur due to various factors. Exploring the ways to predict missing data is needed to ensure the reliability, accuracy, and completeness of datasets for effective decision-making and analysis. This study focused on predicting missing leaf wetness (LW) sensor data using Machine Learning (ML) models, including Multiple Linear Regression (MLR), Support Vector Regression (SVR), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Gradient Boosting (GB), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Random Forest (RF), Deep Neural Network (DNN) and a hybrid stacked model. Cross-validation and correlation were performed for feature selection to select significant variables and interactions. Several environmental parameters, including temperature (T; ˚C), humidity (H; %), soil moisture (SM; %), rainfall (R; mm), rain event (RE) and their interactions (R x T, R x H, R x SM) were used to predict the LW through ML models. To overcome the limitations of traditional methods in handling the spatial and temporal complexity of environmental data, a hybrid stacked machine learning model, which integrates the strengths of RF (for robust imputation on interaction terms) and DNN (for capturing complex patterns) with dropout for L1 and L2 regularization techniques, was tested. The RF model performed better in training with a low Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 0.032, a high R2 of 0.967 and a Kling-Gupta Efficiency (KGE) of 0.919 but failed to capture LW peaks. DNN and Fused Regularized DNN (FDNN) showed moderate MSE (AM: 0.46, 0.45; PM: 0.33,0.49) and satisfactory R2 (AM: 0.53, 0.54; PM: 0.66,0.50), KGE (AM: 0.54, 0.61; PM: 0.7, 0.56), but slightly underestimated LW in training dataset. FDNN performed well compared to RF and DNN in testing data sets, while the hybrid model outperformed other ML models. Through evaluation, it was observed that the hybrid ML model significantly outperformed individual models in both training and validation phases, achieving lower MSE (training = 0.002, validation = 0.113), higher R2 (training = 0.963, validation = 0.887), and improved KGE (training = 0.968, validation = 0.848). This ensemble modeling approach improves the accuracy of gap-filling in LW data and contributes to precise agricultural decision-making and management practices.

title: Dielectric feature-driven dual prediction of moisture content and bulk density for rice quality assessment
abstract: Rapid and accurate determination of moisture content and bulk density in rice is essential for quality assessment, storage, and processing in the agri-food industry. In this study, a microwave-based sensing system was developed to simultaneously predict both moisture content and bulk density in rice cultivars using dielectric parameters as input features. Key dielectric features, including phase shift (ϕ), attenuation (A), dielectric constant (ε’), loss factor (ε’’), and loss tangent (tanδ), were measured in the frequency range of 2–4 GHz. The nine machine learning regressors were implemented to develop predictive models, and their performance was comprehensively evaluated. The k-nearest neighbors and random forest models exhibited the highest predictive accuracy. The models achieved high accuracy in predicting moisture content (correlation coefficient (R) = 0.98, root mean square error (RMSE) = 0.015–0.024) and the most significant results for bulk density (R = 0.92, RMSE = 0.600–1.200). These findings provide potentially encouraging routes for integrating the method into larger digital-agriculture systems and state-of-the-art data storage infrastructure.

title: Automated yield monitor data post-processing pipeline via explainable model benchmarking and stacked ensemble
abstract: Accurate yield data post-processing is a key component of agricultural field management and precision farming analyses. Traditional approaches to post-processing yield monitor data rely on rule-based filtering, manual inspection, and thresholding, which is time-consuming, inconsistent, and relies on expert knowledge. This study demonstrates the viability of machine learning for automated, non-expert detection of erroneous data points, thereby increasing the scalability of yield map generation from raw yield monitor data. Historical yield data (4.6 million data points) were collected from 326 soybean and corn fields in the Delta region of Mississippi. Extensive feature engineering was conducted to derive spatial, operational, and geometric features to enrich model learning. Eight machine learning algorithms (Decision Tree, Random Forest, XGBoost, CatBoost, K-Nearest Neighbors, Artificial Neural Network, Naïve Bayes, and SGDClassifier) were trained with Bayesian-optimized hyperparameters and evaluated across multiple resampling strategies. CatBoost emerged as the best performing model on the raw feature set, achieving an F1-score of 0.77. Random Forest (F1 = 0.76), XGBoost (F1 = 0.74), and Decision Tree (F1 = 0.72) also performed competitively on the raw dataset, though they fell slightly short of CatBoost’s score. Evaluation on unseen fields demonstrated the model’s ability to locate error-prone regions, though isolated false negatives were observed. A stacked ensemble model using XGBoost as the meta -learner slightly improved F1-score (0.78), but gains were limited by high prediction correlation among top base learners and the suboptimal performance of weaker classifiers. SHAP-based interpretation of CatBoost and XGBoost revealed that their predictions aligned well with the domain knowledge.

title: A method for detecting the operational quality of tobacco harvesters based on digital twin and an improved YOLO v10
abstract: Tobacco is an important economic crop, and the operational quality of tobacco harvesters is directly related to the economic benefits and processing quality of tobacco, so it is of great significance to accurately and efficiently detect the problems of missed harvesting tobacco plants, dropped tobacco leaves, and damaged tobacco stems. At present, the traditional manual detection method is inefficient and subjective, which is difficult to meet the demand of modern agriculture refined management; although the target detection model based on deep learning is gradually emerging, there is still a lack of specialized detection technology and system for tobacco harvesting. In this study, we propose a tobacco harvesting quality inspection system that integrates the improved YOLOv10 model and digital twin technology. Based on YOLOv10, SPPELAN, SFA, and ASFF modules are integrated and combined with ByteTrack multi-target tracking algorithm to realize accurate identification and stable tracking of operational anomalies. At the same time, the virtual tobacco field environment is constructed based on the digital twin five-dimensional model, and the real-time detection results are mapped to the virtual space, which completes the three-dimensional visualization, accurate positioning, and feedback of the anomaly detection results. The experimental results show that the system has increased mAP@0.5 by 3.31% in operation quality detection, respectively, which significantly improves the level of intelligent detection and management of operation quality problems in the tobacco field, and provides a reliable technical support for the intelligent evaluation of tobacco planting.

title: Dynamic gamma correction-guided CNN for low-light corn tassel enhancement in intelligent detasselling systems
abstract: The accuracy of intelligent corn detasselling systems is severely compromised by low-light conditions, which degrade image quality and impede tassel recognition. To address the limitations of existing methods, such as noise amplification, detail distortion, and inadequate global illumination modeling, a Low-Light Corn Plant Image Enhancement Model (L2CP-IEM) is proposed. The core of L2CP-IEM is an innovative closed-loop dynamic gamma correction mechanism. This mechanism, guided by the discriminator’s confidence, is embedded within a residual encoder-decoder architecture, enabling adaptive illumination adjustment and stable training. By using a green cardboard calibration method, a high-quality dataset consisting of 950 paired low-light and normal-light corn images was created. Experiments on the LOL-v1 benchmark dataset demonstrate that L2CP-IEM outperforms state-of-the-art methods such as GSAD and CIDNet in terms of the SSIM (0.908) and LPIPS (0.059). Ablation studies further validate the critical roles of residual connections and the dynamic gamma correction mechanism. In practical corn tassel image tests, L2CP-IEM achieves balanced performance in terms of brightness and colour restoration, significantly enhances the reconstruction of natural textures and hierarchical details, and fully restores the confidence of the Mask R-CNN in image segmentation. By synergizing physical principles with data-driven approaches, this method significantly improves the quality of low-light images and the robustness of recognition, thus offering a reliable and efficient solution for agricultural visual automation.

title: Smart turtle farm: soft-shell turtle nesting behavior recognition and monitoring system
abstract: Soft-shell turtle farming, a growing aquaculture practice in East and Southeast Asia, involves a pond habitat and a sand-filled spawning area that serves as a nesting site for female turtles. Harvesting these eggs is a labor-intensive and time-consuming task, as farmers must excavate the entire spawning area to ensure all eggs are collected while avoiding damage to buried eggs. Additionally, turtles may inadvertently nest over existing sites, exposing previously buried eggs to a higher risk of damage or consumption by other turtles. Accurate identification of nest locations can significantly reduce farmers’ workload by eliminating unnecessary excavation, while early detection of exposed eggs allows for timely collection, minimizing egg loss, and improving productivity. To address these challenges, we present a real-time AI-based monitoring system to detect soft-shell turtle nesting behavior and exposed eggs. The system integrates YOLOv7 for detecting turtles and exposed eggs, object tracking to monitor turtle movements, and an LSTM-based spatio-temporal model to recognize nesting behaviors. YOLOv7 achieved an average precision (AP) of 98.9% for turtle detection and 88.8% for exposed egg detection, while the LSTM-based model demonstrated 95.73% accuracy and 98.64% recall for recognizing nesting activity. During the 2022 nesting season, spanning 245 days, the system identified 1,713 nests and saved 76.62% of the egg-harvesting efforts, as farmers no longer needed to excavate the entire spawning site. This efficient, non-invasive approach minimizes egg loss, optimizes farm management, and highlights the potential of precision livestock technologies to enhance productivity and sustainability in soft-shell turtle farming.

title: Monitoring vertical SPAD distribution of winter wheat using UAV cross-circle oblique photography
abstract: Timely acquisition of crop chlorophyll contents is essential for effective field management decisions and comprehensive crop nutritional monitoring. Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) has been extensively utilized for canopy chlorophyll content monitoring. However, prior studies predominantly concentrated on the horizontal variability of SPAD, with few researches dedicated to monitoring the vertical distribution of SPAD. This study aimed to develop a high-resolution vertical SPAD distribution model for winter wheat by integrating UAV-based Cross-Circle Oblique (CCO) photography with the Structure from Motion (SFM) and Multi-View Stereo (MVS) methods. The canopy was divided into upper, middle, and lower layers based on plant height. Nadir and CCO photography were used to capture images, with Nadir photography constructing the upper canopy SPAD model and CCO data used for the vertical distribution model (including upper, middle and lower layers). Shapley values were applied to evaluate feature importance in different machine learning models (GBR, gradient boosting regression; RF, random forest; SVM, support vector machine; RR, ridge regression). Finally, a vertical SPAD distribution model for winter wheat was created with a 0.1-meter gradient. The results demonstrated that the accuracy of SPAD vertical distribution inversion using single machine learning algorithms (KNN: k-nearest neighbor, RR: ridge regression) was lower than that achieved by ensemble learning methods (stacking, RF: random forest). Ensemble learning enhanced R2 and RMSE by 0.13 and 1.23 for the training set, and by 0.09 and 0.56 for the test set, respectively. CCO photography exhibited high accuracy in capturing the SPAD spatiotemporal distribution of winter wheat, with R2 values for the training sets across all three growth stages surpassing 0.8, and R2 values for the test sets ranging from 0.6 to 0.81. The highest accuracy in SPAD vertical distribution inversion was achieved during the heading stage, with R2 and RMSE values for the training and test sets of 0.89, 2.58, and 0.80, 3.34, respectively. Therefore, UAV-based CCO photography combined with the SFM-MVS algorithm demonstrates preliminary potential for vertical SPAD phenotyping and precision nutrient management; however, further validation across different growing seasons and wheat varieties is necessary to confirm its broad generalizability.

title: A fusion framework for orchard heterogeneous images based on M-Unet semantic segmentation and transform-spatial domain
abstract: In complex orchard environments, to address the issue of reduced image quality resulting from the interaction between the foreground and background in apple heterogeneous image fusion, this paper proposes a heterogeneous image fusion framework based on modified U-net (M−Unet) semantic segmentation and transform-spatial domain. There are three modules in this framework, including parameter optimization plugin, semantic segmentation module, and transform-spatial domain fusion module. First, we propose a modified segmentation model named as M−Unet to semantically segment the source image and obtain foreground and background images. Then, the foreground and background images are subjected to Nonsubsampled Shearlet Transform (NSST) decomposition to obtain high-frequency and low-frequency subbands, respectively. Next, the high-frequency and low-frequency subbands are fused for the first time using weighted local energy (WLE) and weighted sum of eight-neighborhood-based modified Laplacian (WSEML). Subsequently, the high-frequency branch is fused by the optimized Parameter-Adaptive Pulse Coupled Neural Network (PAPCNN) model, and the low-frequency branch is fused by WLE and WSEML rule. Afterwards, the inverse NSST transform is operated to obtain the fused image of transform domain. Ultimately, this fused image and the original images are blended using a bilateral filter (BF) and a weighted least squares (WLS) optimization framework. It is the secondary spatial domain fusion to acquire the ultimate fused image. Experiments on two public datasets and one self-built dataset showed that the improved image fusion framework has significant advantages in orchard image fusion. Compared to other fusion algorithms, this fusion framework displays good performance on the detailed expression, clarity, and edge contour details of the image. It demonstrates that the fusion effect is improved by fusing the segmented images in transform domain and the source image in spatial domain. In addition, this study integrates the modular design of the framework, which has the characteristics of high cohesion and low coupling, making it easy to update and replace the modules.

title: An LED-based multispectral discrete spectrometer for in-situ soil moisture sensing using machine learning algorithms
abstract: Accurate, low-cost, and field-deployable soil moisture content (SMC) sensing remains a key challenge in precision agriculture and environmental monitoring. This study presents a compact and energy-efficient approach for in-situ SMC estimation using discrete near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy combined with machine-learning (ML) algorithms. For this purpose, a portable transfer-standard sensor was developed using seven selected NIR light-emitting diodes (LEDs), targeting strong water absorption bands (970, 1150, 1450, and 1900 nm) and weak-absorption reference wavelengths (1100, 1300, and 1650 nm) for soil reflectance measurements. The optomechanical design complies with international soil reflectance spectroscopy standards, employing nadir illumination and 45° detection geometry, while enabling direct comparability between laboratory and field measurements. SI-traceable calibration was performed using thermogravimetric methods over an SMC range from dry conditions to approximately 25% below saturation, utilizing more than ten soil types with varying composition and texture. Linear physical models based on relative absorption depth showed good performance under soil-specific calibration but degraded under heterogeneous field conditions, highlighting sensitivity to soil texture and composition properties. To address this limitation, six ML regression models were evaluated using stratified K-fold cross-validation, feature selection, and normalization. All ML models outperformed the physical approach, with Gaussian Process Regression achieving the highest accuracy, yielding errors below 0.5% for soil-specific calibration and below 2% under generalized field conditions, in agreement with gravimetric references. Wavelength subset analysis revealed diminishing returns beyond five LEDs, with a combination of strong and weak absorption bands providing the most informative feature set. Overall, the results demonstrate that LED-based discrete NIR spectroscopy integrated with ML offers a robust, scalable, and cost- and energy-efficient alternative to conventional spectroscopic systems for in-situ soil moisture monitoring.

title: Soybean drought recognition method based on multi-view 3D image Fourier transform
abstract: Drought stress is an important adversity factor for soybean production. Accurate determination of drought is significant for water-saving irrigation and management. Existing low-cost 3D imaging technology based on Kinect sensors can capture the structural and phenotypic changes of plant canopies, but it is difficult to characterize the relationship between the spectral features of soybean 3D images and environmental factors changes. Thus, in this study, a soybean drought recognition method was proposed based on multi-view 3D image Fourier transform. First, the multi-view projection algorithm of the 3D point cloud was used to obtain 21 view projection images based on the depth and color information of the soybean canopy. Second, a discrete Fourier transform was performed to calculate the frequency-domain features of the images in each projection direction. In addition, a quantum genetic algorithm (QGA) was applied to obtain the optimal combination of feature weights. Finally, the features of the optimal projection images were extracted to establish the drought recognition model of soybeans based on a radial basis function (RBF) neural network. The result showed that the model’s recognition accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score were 95.75%, 95.70%, 91.70%, and 93.60%, respectively, and the four evaluation indexes have been improved by 8.39%, 11.57%, 0.2%, and 5.83%, respectively, compared with the back propagation (BP), random forest (RF), and support vector machine (SVM) methods. This research realized rapid and non-destructive detection of drought stress for the soybean plant, and provided a relevant basis and support for soybean water-saving irrigation and cultivation management.

title: TSA-GAIN method for greenhouse environment data imputation based on encoder and dynamic hint matrix
abstract: Missing data in greenhouse environmental monitoring may substantially compromise the accuracy of predictive models and the effectiveness of control strategies. To address long-gap missing data and the fragmentation of cross-sensor coupling features in greenhouse environmental datasets, this study improves the Generative Adversarial Imputation Network (GAIN) and proposes a Two-Stage Adaptive Generative Adversarial Imputation Network (TSA-GAIN). The main innovations are as follows: an adaptive hint-rate function is designed to optimize the missing-value localization guidance mechanism. By leveraging the dynamic balance between generator and discriminator adversarial losses, the hint rate is updated adaptively, replacing the fixed hint-rate setting in conventional GAIN and thereby constructing a dynamic hint matrix to improve the training process. In addition, the model architecture is enhanced by introducing an encoder module at the front end of the generator. By embedding the distributional characteristics of the original data and the spatiotemporal correlations among variables into the latent noise vector, the model can generate samples more realistically and more stably, effectively addressing the slow convergence and unstable imputation caused by GAIN’s reliance on random noise. Experimental results show that TSA-GAIN significantly outperforms GAIN on three imputation metrics, with MAE reduced by 51.8%, RMSE reduced by 48.7%, and the correlation coefficient increased by 61.7%. Moreover, under high missing rates, the proposed method outperforms traditional approaches such as RF, KNN, and MICE, which can better adapt to the nonlinear relationship in greenhouse climate characteristics.

title: A lightweight, few-shot ready embedding framework for cattle identification using retinal images
abstract: Precise livestock identification is central to modern livestock management system. It enables health surveillance, supporting insurance and liability verification, and ensuring transparency in trade and market transactions of livestock. Various biometric modalities have been explored for bovines such as muzzles, face, coat pattern and retinal imaging. However, retinal imaging offers distinct advantages with its inherent stability and unique vascular structure. This study proposes a lightweight and few-shot ready embedding framework for cattle identification using retinal images that comprises four main components: (1) a lightweight convolutional neural network backbone for retinal feature extraction, (2) a parameter free attention mechanism to enhance feature representations without increasing model complexity, (3) a triplet Siamese network architecture with hard negative mining function to further enhance a discriminative feature learning, and (4) a few-shot identification module that employs cosine distance to compare a query sample against a single image support set. The proposed method highlights the design that operate effectively even when only two labeled images per animal are available for enrollment and verification. This makes it suitable for data constrained retinal biometric cattle identification scenarios. Our method demonstrates identification accuracy of 97.40% under low data regimes while maintaining a compact model size of 4.4MB and an inference latency of 15ms. In addition, the study enhances transparency in the proposed cattle biometrics by providing interpretable insights into the learned representations through explainability and interpretability tools, such as Grad-CAM and t-SNE visualizations, respectively.

title: Simple but effective unsupervised classification for specified domain images: a case study on fungi images
abstract: High-quality labeled datasets are essential for deep learning. Traditional manual annotation methods are not only costly and inefficient but also pose challenges in specialized domains where expert knowledge is needed. Self-supervised methods, despite leveraging unlabeled data for feature extraction, still require hundreds or thousands of labeled instances to guide the model for effective specialized image classification. Current unsupervised learning methods offer automatic classification without prior annotation but often compromise on accuracy. As a result, efficiently procuring high-quality labeled datasets remains a pressing challenge for specialized domain images devoid of annotated data. Addressing this, an unsupervised classification method with three key ideas is introduced: 1) dual-step feature dimensionality reduction using a pre-trained model and manifold learning, 2) a voting mechanism from multiple clustering algorithms, and 3) post-hoc instead of prior manual annotation. Using fungal image data as an example, the results show that, after rejecting some ambiguous samples, the proposed method outperformed supervised learning methods in classification accuracy, achieving accuracies of 94.1 % and 96.7 % on the public and private datasets, respectively. The proposed unsupervised classification method reduces dependency on pre-annotated datasets, enabling a closed-loop for data classification. The simplicity and ease of use of this method will also bring convenience to researchers in various fields in building datasets, promoting AI applications for images in specialized domains.

title: From sensing to modeling: machine learning-driven wearable humidity sensors for plant water status monitoring
abstract: Plant water status is a critical phenotypic trait underlying precision agriculture and crop health assessment. Yet, continuous, in situ, and non-invasive monitoring under field conditions remains challenging due to limitations in sensor adhesion stability, environmental interference, and the complexity of interpreting sensor signals. Flexible wearable humidity sensors that can attach to leaf and stem surfaces provide real-time access to near-surface moisture dynamics and transpiration activity. As these sensors generate high-dimensional, strongly coupled, and nonlinear datasets, machine learning has emerged as a promising tool for extracting features and predicting plant water status. However, practical deployment faces obstacles such as signal drift, environmental noise, and biofouling, while model generalizability and interpretability remain key barriers to widespread adoption. This review first systematically outlines the physiological mechanisms governing plant water regulation and summarizes recent advances in materials and device innovations for wearable humidity sensors. It then critically examines the integration of machine learning in sensor data analysis and modeling. Finally, we propose a unified conceptual framework that bridges plant water regulation, sensor-based perception, and data-driven analysis, highlighting how algorithmic strategies can enhance system robustness and enable multiscale characterization. This framework lays a theoretical foundation for intelligent monitoring and precision regulation under real-world agricultural conditions.
